He also experimented with various different vocal styles, ranging from light [[falsetto]], to high falsetto screams, and chants. In addition to singing rock and metal mainly with Soundgarden and Audioslave, Cornell sang [[blues]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Recordings Chris Cornell Euphoria Morning (A&M/Interscope)|author=McCormick, Moira|newspaper=Chicago Tribune|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/1999-10-03/news/9910030151_1_euphoria-morning-flutter-girl-soundgarden|date=October 3, 1999|url-status=dead|archive-url=http://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/20140115123731/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/1999-10-03/news/9910030151_1_euphoria-morning-flutter-girl-soundgarden|archive-date=January 15, 2014}}</ref> [[neo soul]]<ref name="npr"/> and stripped-down acoustic numbers.<ref>{{cite news|title=Chris Cornell's one man show|author=Masley, Ed|publisher=MesaArtsCenter|url=http://www.mesaartscenter.com/sysfile/file-325c0fee2def61c93043f3865922e305-file.pdf|date=August 12, 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116103415/http://www.mesaartscenter.com/sysfile/file-325c0fee2def61c93043f3865922e305-file.pdf|archive-date=January 16, 2014}}</ref> ''[[The New York Times]]'' music critic [[Jon Pareles]] wrote, "As it rose, higher and higher, Mr. Cornell's voice could sustain a melody through the fray, or it could confront hard-rock turbulence with grunts, rasps, wails, bitter moans and, at the top of his range, full-bodied shrieks that admitted no weakness."<ref name="Pareles2017-05-18"/>

==Other work==
Cornell made a cameo in the 1992 Seattle-based film ''[[Singles (1992 film)|Singles]]'' directed by [[Cameron Crowe]], in which he appeared opposite [[Matt Dillon]] and [[Bridget Fonda]].<ref name="Singles cameo">{{YouTube|id=7J5H8YzfARE|title=Chris Cornell's cameo in "Singles"}}</ref> He also appeared onstage with Soundgarden performing the song "Birth Ritual" in a club. Cornell was Crowe's original choice for the role of Cliff Poncier (played by Dillon), but he was unable to do it due to Soundgarden's busy schedule.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/cameron-crowe-on-the-singles-soundtrack-chris-cornell-194903/ |title=Cameron Crowe on the 'Singles' Soundtrack, Chris Cornell |last=Sottile |first=Alexis |date=May 18, 2017 |magazine=Rolling Stone}}</ref> Cornell was the face of fashion producer [[John Varvatos]]' 2006&nbsp;ad campaign.<ref name="Varvatos">{{cite web |url=https://www.johnvarvatos.com/worldofjohnvarvatoscontent?cid=ss06campaign |title=Spring/Summer 2006 Campaign |access-date=May 18, 2017 |work=John Varvatos |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729141258/https://www.johnvarvatos.com/worldofjohnvarvatoscontent?cid=ss06campaign |archive-date=July 29, 2017}}</ref>

Cornell became a restaurateur with the opening of his restaurant, Black Calavados, in Paris,<ref name="stout"/> and was also the owner of the music publishing company ''You Make Me Sick I Make Music''.<ref name="discogs">{{cite web |url=https://www.discogs.com/label/267221-You-Make-Me-Sick-I-Make-Music |title=You Make Me Sick I Make Music |access-date=May 18, 2017 |work=Discogs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809155622/https://www.discogs.com/label/267221-You-Make-Me-Sick-I-Make-Music |archive-date=August 9, 2017}}</ref>

In 2009, Cornell planned to turn [[Philip Carlo]]'s true crime book ''The Night Stalker: The Life and Crimes of [[Richard Ramirez]]'', into a film, collaborating with Carlo to produce the screenplay.<ref name="New York Press">{{cite web|url=http://www.nypress.com/blog-5098-chop-shop-phil-carlo-on-gruesome-murder-and-chatting-with-serial-killers.html|title=Chop Shop: Phil Carlo on Gruesome Murder and Chatting with Serial Killers|last=Rathe|first=Adam|date=September 23, 2009|publisher=New York Press|access-date=October 7, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090926051205/http://www.nypress.com/blog-5098-chop-shop-phil-carlo-on-gruesome-murder-and-chatting-with-serial-killers.html|archive-date=September 26, 2009}}</ref> In 2011, [[James Franco]] was attached to direct the film and star in the role of Ramirez.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2011/01/james-franco-to-direct-star-in-serial-killer-tale-the-night-stalker-120862/ |title=James Franco To Direct & Star In Serial Killer Tale 'The Night Stalker' |work=IndieWire |date=January 17, 2011 |access-date=June 9, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180423170151/http://www.indiewire.com/2011/01/james-franco-to-direct-star-in-serial-killer-tale-the-night-stalker-120862/ |archive-date=April 23, 2018}}</ref>

==In popular culture==
[[Garbage (band)|Garbage]]'s song "Fix Me Now" from [[Garbage (album)|the band's debut album]] was originally called "Chris Cornell". According to lead singer [[Shirley Manson]], she was obsessed with Cornell at the time of the release of Soundgarden's hit song "[[Black Hole Sun]]". A demo version of "Fix Me Now" has Manson singing Cornell's name.<ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211211/hRgSlL2n0HY Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20181215141659/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hRgSlL2n0HY Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hRgSlL2n0HY |title=Shirley Manson Reveals That Garbage's Song 'Fix Me Now' Was Originally Called 'Chris Cornell' |website=YouTube|date=March 6, 2018 |access-date=March 14, 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

The line "I'm looking California, and feeling Minnesota" from Soundgarden's song "[[Outshined]]" (written by Cornell), inspired the title of [[Steven Baigelman]]'s 1996 film ''[[Feeling Minnesota]]'', starring [[Keanu Reeves]] and [[Cameron Diaz]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/lists/chris-cornell-15-essential-songs-w482883/soundgarden-outshined-1991-w482893|title=Chris Cornell: 15 Essential Songs – Soundgarden, "Outshined" (1991)|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=May 18, 2017|access-date=November 9, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110005426/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/lists/chris-cornell-15-essential-songs-w482883/soundgarden-outshined-1991-w482893|archive-date=November 10, 2017}}</ref>

Cornell's song "Preaching the End of the World" from his debut solo album ''[[Euphoria Morning]]'', inspired the title of [[Lorene Scafaria]]'s 2012 film ''[[Seeking a Friend for the End of the World]]'', starring [[Steve Carell]] and [[Keira Knightley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/commentary-norah-had-screenwriter-wanting-120281|title=Commentary: 'Norah' had screenwriter wanting to be 16 again|work=The Hollywood Reporter|date=October 2, 2008|access-date=November 9, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171109193255/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/commentary-norah-had-screenwriter-wanting-120281|archive-date=November 9, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/entertainment/movies/for-end-of-the-world-writerdirector-lorene-scafaria-music-is-key/2012/06/21/gJQAXGfetV_story.html|title=For 'End of the World' writer/director Lorene Scafaria, music is key|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=June 21, 2012|access-date=November 9, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170821093936/https://www.washingtonpost.com/entertainment/movies/for-end-of-the-world-writerdirector-lorene-scafaria-music-is-key/2012/06/21/gJQAXGfetV_story.html|archive-date=August 21, 2017}}</ref>

|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170602235157/http://web.stargate.net/soundgarden/misc/ssilver.shtml |archive-date=June 2, 2017}}</ref> the manager of [[Alice in Chains]], [[Soundgarden]], and [[Screaming Trees]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19910106/1259221/faces-to-watch-in-91 |title=Faces To Watch In '91 -- A Look At Up-And-Comers Who Will Be Helping |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170522230732/http://people.com/music/chris-cornell-life-influential-seattle-scene/ |archive-date=May 22, 2017}}</ref><ref name="Silver">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/7800264/chris-cornell-obit |title=Chris Cornell, Singer with Soundgarden and Audioslave, Dies at 52 |access-date=May 18, 2017 |magazine=Billboard |date=May 18, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170518092406/http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/7800264/chris-cornell-obit |archive-date=May 18, 2017}}</ref> They had a daughter, born on June 28, 2000.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chris Cornell Feels "Euphoria" With Newborn Daughter|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1427500/chris-cornell-feels-euphoria-with-newborn-daughter/|website=MTV|access-date=August 3, 2017|date=July 6, 2000|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170804053242/http://www.mtv.com/news/1427500/chris-cornell-feels-euphoria-with-newborn-daughter/|archive-date=August 4, 2017}}</ref> Cornell and Silver divorced in 2004.<ref name="Silver"/>

In 2004, he married Vicky Karayiannis,<ref>{{cite news|title=Cornell Loses $30,000 in Argentine Flood |url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/blogs/sfgate/category?blogid=7&cat=1022 |newspaper=San Francisco Chronicle |access-date=April 4, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080328041113/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/blogs/sfgate/category?blogid=7&cat=1022 |archive-date=March 28, 2008}}</ref> a Paris-based American publicist of Greek heritage.<ref name="stout"/> The couple had a daughter together, [[Toni Cornell|Toni]], in September 2004,<ref name="Silver"/><ref name="stout"/> and a son, born in December 2005.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chris Cornell's wife has a baby|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1517554/20051206/audioslave.jhtml|publisher=MTV|access-date=April 11, 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511092418/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1517554/20051206/audioslave.jhtml|archive-date=May 11, 2008}}</ref> In 2012, the Cornells created the Chris and Vicky Cornell Foundation<ref name="CVCF">{{cite web |url=https://www.globalcitizen.org/en/content/chris-cornell-global-citizen-soundgarden-audioslav/ |title=Chris Cornell Was a Rock Star and a Global Citizen |access-date=May 18, 2017 |work=Global Citizen |date=May 18, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170708025551/https://www.globalcitizen.org/en/content/chris-cornell-global-citizen-soundgarden-audioslav/ |archive-date=July 8, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.citizenaudit.org/organization/461543070/CHRIS%20AND%20VICKY%20CORNELL%20FOUNDATION/ |title=Chris & Vicky Cornell Foundation |work=CitizenAudit.org |access-date=May 31, 2017}}</ref> which works to aid the homeless, the poor, and abused or neglected children. In 2013, a portion of proceeds from ticket sales went to benefit the cause.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/chris-cornell-tries-a-new-voice/ |title=Chris Cornell tries a new voice |work=[[The Seattle Times]] |first=Nicole |last=Brodeur |date=October 13, 2013 |access-date=May 18, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170602163843/http://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/chris-cornell-tries-a-new-voice/ |archive-date=June 2, 2017}}</ref>

In a 2008 television interview, Cornell said about religion, "I don't follow any particular one. ... Ultimately I think I'm sort of a [[Freethought|freethinker]] and kind of open. ... So many bad things–as well as good things–have happened based on people just sort of blindly following religion that I kind of feel like I want to stay away from any type of specific denomination or any religion period."<ref name="religion">Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211211/NGtbjYezJ8g Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20130302052558/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NGtbjYezJ8g Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NGtbjYezJ8g&t=4m3s |title=THE STANDARD chris cornell#2 |website=YouTube |date=March 30, 2008 |access-date=May 26, 2017}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He became a [[Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople|Greek Orthodox Christian]] during his relationship with Karayiannis.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-05-24 |title=The Prayers of Chris Cornell |url=https://www.americamagazine.org/arts-culture/2017/05/24/prayers-chris-cornell |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=[[America (magazine)|America]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-05-19 |title=Chris Cornell: Soundgarden singer who helped define grunge |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/chris-cornell-soungarden-obituary-grunge-seattle-a7744616.html |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2017-05-19 |title=Dynamic Performer Chris Cornell Dies Aged 52 |url=https://greekcitytimes.com/2017/05/19/dynamic-performer-chris-cornell-dies-aged-52/ |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=Greek City Times |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=admin |date=2017-05-20 |title=Vicky (Karayiannis), Chris Cornell's Greek Wife, Disputes He Killed Himself |url=https://www.thenationalherald.com/vicky-karayiannis-chris-cornells-greek-wife-disputes-he-killed-himself/ |access-date=2025-01-29 |website=[[The National Herald]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Friendships with Andrew Wood and Eddie Vedder===
Cornell was a close friend of late singer [[Andrew Wood (singer)|Andrew Wood]], who was his roommate in Seattle.<ref name="roommate"/> While living together, they recorded the song "Island of Summer",<ref name="Island of Summer">{{YouTube|id=FVzNIfDdn4I |title=Chris Cornell – Island Of Summer (With Andrew Wood)}}</ref> which was written by Cornell and is the only existing recording of the two of them singing together. The song was released in 2011 in the album ''Melodies & Dreams'', a solo album from Andrew Wood featuring unreleased songs he recorded throughout his life. Wood's sudden death in 1990 led Cornell to make a [[tribute album]] for him with the band [[Temple of the Dog]]. In a 2016 interview with ''[[The Guardian]]'' promoting the first tour of Temple of the Dog, Cornell said about Wood's death: "I've always had a really difficult time with loss. I didn't deal well with Andy's death. After he died, numerous times I'd be driving and I would look out the window and I thought I saw him. It would take me five minutes to update to the moment and realize, 'no, he's actually dead.' This tour, in a sense, is the dealing. It's facing the reality."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2016/nov/16/temple-of-the-dog-chris-cornell-eddie-vedder-90s-grunge |title=Temple of the Dog: Chris Cornell on the return of the 90s grunge supergroup |website=The Guardian |date=November 16, 2016 |access-date=May 31, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170527030543/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2016/nov/16/temple-of-the-dog-chris-cornell-eddie-vedder-90s-grunge |archive-date=May 27, 2017}}</ref>

During a 1994 ''Rolling Stone'' interview on [[Kurt Cobain]]'s suicide, when asked if it is legitimate to read a songwriter's suicide into his lyrics after the fact, Cornell said:{{blockquote|When Andy [Wood] died, I couldn't listen to his songs for about two years after that, and it was for that reason—his lyrics often seem as though they can tell that story. But then again, my lyrics often could tell the same one. In terms of seeing everything as a matter of life and death—if that's what you're feeling at the time, then that's what you're going to write. It's sort of a morbid exchange when somebody who is a writer like that dies, and then everyone starts picking through all their lyrics. In Kurt's case, whatever he was thinking and whatever he was writing, there wasn't an arrow pointing at what his demise was. It's a stream of thought, it's a possibility—it's definitely something that somebody was feeling when they were writing. It doesn't mean that it's going to happen. But it doesn't necessarily mean that it isn't, either.<ref name="Rolling Stone 1994">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/the-rolling-stone-interview-chris-cornell-19941229 |title=Chris Cornell: The Rolling Stone Interview |author=Alec Foege |magazine=Rolling Stone |date=December 29, 1994 |access-date=May 31, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170601043445/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/the-rolling-stone-interview-chris-cornell-19941229 |archive-date=June 1, 2017}}</ref>}}

Cornell was good friends with [[Pearl Jam]] frontman [[Eddie Vedder]]. Cornell was one of the first people that Vedder met outside his Pearl Jam bandmates after moving to Seattle in 1990.<ref name="PJ20 2011">{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GbG9CNCettk |title=Pearl Jam Chris Cornell *Hunger Strike* PJ20 night 2 @ Alpine Valley Temple of the Dog 9/4/2011 HD |work=YouTube |date=September 5, 2011 |access-date=June 6, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170626092242/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GbG9CNCettk |archive-date=June 26, 2017}}</ref> The two were neighbors for a while and shared vocal duties in Temple of the Dog.<ref name="PJ20 2011"/> Soundgarden manager Susan Silver recalled in the 2009 book ''Grunge Is Dead: The Oral History of Seattle Rock Music'' the moment in 1990 that Cornell walked Vedder onstage at the second show performed by Pearl Jam (then Mookie Blaylock) in Seattle: "Alice in Chains filmed the show at Moore theatre in 1990 and that was the show this new band [Mookie Blaylock] opened for them. Everyone was still reeling from Andy [Andrew Wood]'s death... and they hadn't really played out yet. The band came on and Chris carried Eddie onto the stage – he was on his shoulders. It was one of those super powerful moments, where it was all a big healing for everybody. He came out as this guy who had all the credibility in the world – in terms of people in Seattle – and Malfunkshun and Mother Love Bone were loved bands. Andy was such an endearing personality. It was a hard thing to do – to show up after people die. And Chris bringing Eddie out, and pointing at him, as much to say, 'This is your guy now.'"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.seattleweekly.com/music/how-chris-cornell-shaped-seattle-music/ |title=How Chris Cornell Shaped Seattle Music |author=Clint Brownlee |website=Seattle Weekly |date=May 22, 2017 |access-date=June 6, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170606081104/http://www.seattleweekly.com/music/how-chris-cornell-shaped-seattle-music/ |archive-date=June 6, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eTg4whS9ClUC&q=credibility |title=Grunge Is Dead: The Oral History of Seattle Rock Music, 2009 |access-date=June 6, 2017|isbn=9781554903474 |last1=Prato |first1=Greg |date=December 15, 2010|publisher=ECW Press }}</ref> Pearl Jam lead guitarist Mike McCready said about their friendship; "Ed was from San Diego and he felt very intimidated in Seattle. Chris really welcomed him. Ed was super, super shy. Chris took him out for beers and told him stories. He was like, 'Hey, welcome to Seattle. I love Jeff [Ament] and Stone [Gossard]. I give you my blessing.' From then on, he was more relaxed. It was one of the coolest things I saw Chris do."<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/temple-of-the-dog-an-oral-history-w442502 |title=Temple of the Dog: An Oral History |magazine=Rolling Stone |date=September 30, 2016 |access-date=June 6, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170606164750/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/temple-of-the-dog-an-oral-history-w442502 |archive-date=June 6, 2017}}</ref>

In September 2011, Vedder introduced Cornell at a concert in [[Alpine Valley]] before performing "Hunger Strike" with him, saying, "I had no idea how he would affect my life and my views on music and my views on friendship and what a big impact he would have. These guys [the other members of Pearl Jam] know him much longer than me and his impact is profound."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kiro7.com/news/local/the-day-chris-cornell-and-eddie-vedder-watched-the-kingdome-implosion/527032626 |title=The day Chris Cornell and Eddie Vedder watched the Kingdome implosion |work=Kiro7 |date=May 26, 2017 |access-date=June 6, 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170531004136/http://www.kiro7.com/news/local/the-day-chris-cornell-and-eddie-vedder-watched-the-kingdome-implosion/527032626 |archive-date=May 31, 2017 }}</ref><ref name="PJ20 2011"/> The friendship between Vedder and Cornell is also featured in the 2011 documentary ''[[Pearl Jam Twenty]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://vimeo.com/220127751 |title=Temple of the Dog and the friendship between Chris Cornell and Eddie Vedder |work=Vimeo |access-date=June 9, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171031054811/https://vimeo.com/220127751 |archive-date=October 31, 2017}}</ref>

===Depression and substance abuse===
Cornell struggled with depression<ref name="Rolling Stone 1992"/><ref name="Rolling Stone 2014">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/soundgardens-chris-cornell-on-superunknown-depression-w483113 |title=Soundgarden's Chris Cornell on 'Superunknown,' Depression and Kurt Cobain |magazine=Rolling Stone |date=May 19, 2017 |access-date=June 9, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170611161550/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/soundgardens-chris-cornell-on-superunknown-depression-w483113 |archive-date=June 11, 2017}}</ref><ref name="People"/> and had multiple addictions<ref name="Rolling Stone 1994"/><ref name="People"/><ref name=addict/> that he was able to manage until 1997, when Soundgarden disbanded and his first marriage was failing.<ref name="Guardian"/> At that point, Cornell turned to [[oxycodone]] and other substances.<ref name="Guardian"/> He said of that period: "I went through a serious crisis with depression where I didn't eat a whole meal every day. I was just kind of shutting down. I eventually found that the only way out of that was to change virtually everything in my life. That was a very frightening thing to do, but it was worthwhile."<ref name="stout"/> He checked into a rehabilitation center in 2002<ref name="Metal"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.spin.com/2003/06/come-clean/ |title=Come Clean |website=Spin |date=June 23, 2003 |access-date=May 31, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170523083015/http://www.spin.com/2003/06/come-clean/ |archive-date=May 23, 2017}}</ref> and quit drinking and smoking around 2005.<ref name="Revelations"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.menshealth.com/guy-wisdom/chris-cornell-death-depression-suicide-interview |title=What Chris Cornell Told Me About His Depression Years Before His Suicide |author=Mike Zimmerman |website=Men's Health |date=May 19, 2017 |access-date=May 31, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170523002427/http://www.menshealth.com/guy-wisdom/chris-cornell-death-depression-suicide-interview |archive-date=May 23, 2017}}</ref>

Cornell stated in a 1996 interview: "I know what it feels like to be [[suicidal]], and I know what it feels like to be hopeless. There is some point where I learned enough about myself to know that I don't have the tolerance to create other hurdles as well."<ref name="Metal Hammer 1996">{{cite web|title=Soundgarden – Seattle's Superwellknown|url=http://web.stargate.net/soundgarden/articles/hammer_10-96.shtml|publisher=Metal Hammer|access-date=July 28, 2017|date=October 1996|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150912092845/http://web.stargate.net/soundgarden/articles/hammer_10-96.shtml|archive-date=September 12, 2015}}</ref> In 1999, Cornell said the following about depression:{{blockquote|No one really knows what run-of-the-mill depression is. You'll think somebody has run-of-the-mill depression, and then the next thing you know, they're hanging from a rope. It's hard to tell the difference. But I do feel that depression can be useful. Sometimes it's just chemical. It doesn't seem to come from anywhere. And whenever I've been in any kind of depression, I've over the years tried to not only imagine what it feels like to not be there, but try to remind myself that I could just wake up the next day and it could be gone because that happens, and not to worry about it. And at the same time, when I'm feeling great, I remember the depression and think about the differences in what I'm feeling and why I would feel that way, and not be reactionary one way or the other. You just have to realize that these are patterns of life and you just go through them.<ref name="Guitar World 1999">{{cite web|last1=Wiederhorn|first1=Jon|title=Chris Cornell: A Changed Man.|url=https://www.guitar.com/articles/chris-cornell-changed-man|website=Guitar.com|access-date=July 28, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170616173119/https://www.guitar.com/articles/chris-cornell-changed-man|archive-date=June 16, 2017|date=September 29, 1999}}</ref>}}

At age 12, Cornell had access to alcohol, [[cannabis|marijuana]], and prescription drugs; he used them daily by 13, stopped for a year, but relapsed at 15 for another year until he turned to music.<ref name="Rolling Stone 1994"/><ref name="People"/> In a 2006 interview, Cornell revealed that at age 14, he had a bad [[Phencyclidine|PCP]] experience and later had [[panic disorder]] and [[agoraphobia]]:{{blockquote|It's not like you go to your dad or your doctor and say, 'Yeah, I smoked PCP and I'm having a bad time.' So I became more or less agoraphobic because I'd have flashbacks. From 14 to 16, I didn't have any friends. I stayed home most of the time. Up till then life was pretty great... I never did any drugs until my late 20s. Unfortunately, being a child of two alcoholics, I started drinking a lot, and that's what eventually got me back into drugs. You often hear that pot leads to harder drugs. But I think alcohol is what leads you to everything, because it takes away the fear. The worst drug experimentation I ever did was because I was drunk and didn't care.<ref name=spin />}}

In May 2007, Cornell was honored with the [[Stevie Ray Vaughan|Stevie Ray Vaughan Award]] for "his dedication and support of the [[MusiCares|MusiCares MAP Fund]] and his devotion to helping other addicts with the recovery process."<ref>{{YouTube|id=Y2P3VorpzLE|title=Musicares Honors Chris Cornell, Dave Gahan, With Map Benefit}}</ref> The award was presented by [[Alice Cooper]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/alice-cooper-to-present-stevie-ray-vaughan-award-to-chris-cornell/|title=Alice Cooper To Present Stevie Ray Vaughan Award To CHRIS CORNELL|work=Blabbermouth|date=May 2, 2017|access-date=July 7, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170523055006/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/alice-cooper-to-present-stevie-ray-vaughan-award-to-chris-cornell/|archive-date=May 23, 2017}}</ref>

When asked how he beat his addictions, Cornell stated, {{blockquote|It was a long period of coming to the realization that this way (sober) is better. Going through rehab, honestly, did help... it got me away from just the daily drudgery of depression and either trying to not drink or do drugs or doing them and you know, they give you such a simple message that any idiot can get and it's just over and over, but the bottom line is really, and this is the part that is scary for everyone, the individual kinda has to want it... not kinda, you have to want it and to not do that crap anymore or you will never stop and it will just kill you. There's nothing you can do...if your best friend has a problem and it's very serious, there's nothing you're going to be able to do about it and it was sad for me and the people around me. Sad for me when friends of mine died because of it.<ref name=angelfire>{{cite web|title=Rock N Roll Experience's interview w/ Chris Cornell|url=http://www.angelfire.com/rock/e4/chriscornell.html |website=Angelfire.com|access-date=July 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071121013005/http://www.angelfire.com/rock/e4/chriscornell.html|archive-date=November 21, 2007}}</ref>}}

In a 2011 interview, Cornell said the major change when Soundgarden re-formed was a lack of alcohol: "The biggest difference I noticed... and we haven't even really talked about it: there are no bottles of [[Jack Daniel's]] around or beers. And we never talked about it... it's just not there."<ref>{{cite web|title=3 News New Zealand interview with Chris Cornell|url=http://www.3news.co.nz/Chris-Cornell-talks-Soundgarden-and-life---full-interview/tabid/551/articleID/215669/Default.aspx|website=3news.co.nz|access-date=July 20, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130729084332/http://www.3news.co.nz/Chris-Cornell-talks-Soundgarden-and-life---full-interview/tabid/551/articleID/215669/Default.aspx|archive-date=July 29, 2013}}</ref>

==Death and aftermath==

Around 12:15&nbsp;a.m. on May 18, 2017,<ref name="Spin police report"/> Cornell's bodyguard found him unconscious in the bathroom of his hotel room, 1136 at the [[MGM Grand Detroit|MGM Grand]] in [[Detroit, Michigan]], after performing at a show with Soundgarden at the [[Fox Theatre (Detroit)|Fox Theatre]] on May 17.<ref name="RS police report">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/chris-cornell-police-report-details-singers-death-w483238|title=Chris Cornell: Police Report Details Singer's Final Hours|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=May 19, 2017|access-date=May 20, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170520014146/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/chris-cornell-police-report-details-singers-death-w483238|archive-date=May 20, 2017}}</ref> He was lying on the floor with an [[resistance band|exercise band]] around his neck and blood in his mouth.<ref name="full police report"/> An MGM medic and [[Emergency medical services|EMS]] personnel were unable to revive Cornell.<ref name="Spin police report"/> Cornell was pronounced dead by a doctor at 1:30&nbsp;a.m., at the age of 52. The cause of death was officially ruled a [[suicide by hanging]].<ref name="Spin police report">{{cite web |url=http://www.spin.com/2017/05/chris-cornell-police-report-death-details/ |title=Chris Cornell Police Report Details the Hours Before Singer's Death |first=Taylor |last=Berman |work=Spin |date=May 19, 2017 |access-date=May 21, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170520085544/http://www.spin.com/2017/05/chris-cornell-police-report-death-details/ |archive-date=May 20, 2017}}</ref> Police ruled out [[crime|foul play]] by reviewing a hotel surveillance video, which showed nobody entering or exiting the suite after Cornell's bodyguard left at around 11:35&nbsp;p.m.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/entertainment/music/2017/05/22/chris-cornell-death-investigation/102022312/|title=Police used video to rule out homicide in Cornell case|date=May 22, 2017|newspaper=The Detroit News|access-date=June 13, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170613133719/http://www.detroitnews.com/story/entertainment/music/2017/05/22/chris-cornell-death-investigation/102022312/|archive-date=June 13, 2017}}</ref>

On June 2, 2017, the Wayne County Medical Examiner released its autopsy<ref name="autopsy report">{{cite web|url=https://www.scribd.com/document/350206037/Autopsy-Report-Chris-Cornell|title=Autopsy Report Chris Cornell|publisher=Scribd|date=June 2, 2017|access-date=March 4, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171117173315/https://www.scribd.com/document/350206037/Autopsy-Report-Chris-Cornell|archive-date=November 17, 2017}}</ref> and toxicology report in the death of Cornell.<ref name="toxicology">{{cite web|url=https://www.scribd.com/document/350206045/Toxicology-Report-Chris-Cornell|title=Toxicology Report Chris Cornell|publisher=Scribd|date=June 2, 2017|access-date=March 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200728130341/https://www.scribd.com/document/350206045/Toxicology-Report-Chris-Cornell|archive-date=July 28, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The medical examiner confirmed that the cause of death was hanging and determined the manner of death to be suicide, adding that Cornell's injuries were all "consistent with hanging, partially suspended by the resistance exercise band",<ref name="autopsy report"/> and that "drugs did not contribute" to the cause of death.<ref name="autopsy report"/> Only prescription medications in therapeutic doses were found in Cornell's system:<ref name="toxicology"/> the sedative [[Butalbital]] (5.4&nbsp;μg/mL), commonly prescribed for the treatment of headache; four doses (41&nbsp;ng/mL) of the anti-anxiety medication [[lorazepam]] (also known as Ativan); the decongestant [[pseudoephedrine]] (170&nbsp;ng/mL) and its metabolite [[Cathine|norpseudoephedrine]] (10&nbsp;ng/mL); [[caffeine]] (from [[No-Doz]] tablets that Cornell had ingested);<ref name="toxicology"/><ref name="RS toxicology">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/chris-cornell-autopsy-and-toxicology-report-released-w484309|title=Chris Cornell Autopsy Report: 'Drugs Did Not Contribute' to Death|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=June 2, 2017|access-date=June 3, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170603005906/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/chris-cornell-autopsy-and-toxicology-report-released-w484309|archive-date=June 3, 2017}}</ref> and [[naloxone]] (used to reverse opioid overdoses), which was reportedly administered by emergency personnel upon their arrival at the scene.<ref name="toxicology"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/la-et-entertainment-news-updates-june-toxicology-results-in-chris-cornell-s-1496434177-htmlstory.html|title=Toxicology results shed more light on Chris Cornell's death|work=Los Angeles Times|date=June 2, 2017|access-date=June 3, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170602225201/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/la-et-entertainment-news-updates-june-toxicology-results-in-chris-cornell-s-1496434177-htmlstory.html|archive-date=June 2, 2017}}</ref> No pills were found in Cornell's stomach.<ref name="autopsy report"/> Cornell's widow stated that the lorazepam was prescribed to him in 2016 as a sleep aid.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chris Cornell's Widow Vicky Opens Up About His Addiction Battle and Final Night: 'He Didn't Want to Die'|url=http://people.com/music/chris-cornell-widow-speaks-he-didnt-want-to-die/|website=People.com|access-date=August 5, 2017|date=June 28, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170806100651/http://people.com/music/chris-cornell-widow-speaks-he-didnt-want-to-die/|archive-date=August 6, 2017}}</ref> 
Cornell's widow contacted insurance lawyer Kirk Pasich a few minutes after her husband's death.<ref name="Lawdragon">{{cite web|url=http://www.lawdragon.com/2018/01/08/lawyer-limelight-kirk-pasich/|title=Lawyer Limelight: Kirk Pasich |work=Lawdragon|date=January 8, 2018|access-date=March 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304070856/http://www.lawdragon.com/2018/01/08/lawyer-limelight-kirk-pasich/|archive-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> Pasich became the spokesperson for the widow and blamed lorazepam for the singer's death, stating that Cornell would not intentionally take his own life.<ref name=VarietyInt/><ref name="Lawdragon"/> Cornell's widow said, "When we spoke after the show, I noticed he was slurring his words; he was different. When he told me he may have taken an extra Ativan or two, I contacted security and asked that they check on him."<ref name=VarietyInt>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2017/music/news/chris-cornells-family-prescription-drugs-may-have-influenced-suicide-1202436611/|title=Chris Cornell's Family: Prescription Drugs May Have Influenced Suicide|work=Variety|access-date=May 18, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519120616/http://variety.com/2017/music/news/chris-cornells-family-prescription-drugs-may-have-influenced-suicide-1202436611/|archive-date=May 19, 2017}}</ref><ref name=Billboard>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/chris-cornell-wife-statement-heartbroken-ativan-7800980/|title=Chris Cornell's Wife Says Loss has Created 'Emptiness in My Heart that will Never Be Filled; Questions Cause of Death.|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=May 18, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519135408/http://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/rock/7800980/chris-cornell-wife-statement-heartbroken-ativan|archive-date=May 19, 2017}}</ref> Following the release of the autopsy and toxicology report, Cornell's widow released a statement to the press:

{{blockquote|1=Many of us who know Chris well noticed that he wasn't himself during his final hours and that something was very off. We have learned from this report that several substances were found in his system. After so many years of sobriety, this moment of terrible judgment seems to have completely impaired and altered his state of mind. Something clearly went terribly wrong and my children and I are heartbroken and are devastated that this moment can never be taken back. We very much appreciate all of the love we have received during this extremely difficult time and are dedicated to helping others in preventing this type of tragedy.<ref name="RS toxicology"/>}}

Three weeks after his death, the music video for Cornell's single "[[Nearly Forgot My Broken Heart]]" was removed from YouTube.<ref name="NFMBH">{{cite web |url=http://www.spin.com/2017/06/chris-cornell-noose-music-video-deleted-youtube/ |title=Chris Cornell's Final, Morbid Music Video Has Been Taken Offline |work=Spin |date=June 12, 2017 |access-date=June 16, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170615062226/http://www.spin.com/2017/06/chris-cornell-noose-music-video-deleted-youtube/ |archive-date=June 15, 2017}}</ref> Released in September 2015,<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/chris-cornell-make-acting-debut-in-nearly-forgot-my-broken-beart-video-soundgarden-6693302/ |title=Watch Chris Cornell Make Acting Debut, Escape Death in His New Western-Themed Music Video |magazine=Billboard |date=September 11, 2015 |access-date=June 16, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170218225839/http://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/rock/6693302/chris-cornell-make-acting-debut-in-nearly-forgot-my-broken-beart-video-soundgarden |archive-date=February 18, 2017 }}</ref> the video depicted the singer as a death row prisoner in the [[Old West]] who survived a hanging. Cornell's son, Christopher, also appeared in the video.<ref name="NFMBH"/>

Cornell publicly talked about his struggle with depression, isolation, and suicidal thoughts several times throughout his life.<ref name="Metal Hammer 1996"/><ref name="Guitar World 1999"/><ref name="Rolling Stone 1992"/><ref name="People"/><ref name="Rolling Stone 2014"/><ref name="Rolling Stone 1994"/> This started after Cornell stated he had ingested [[Phencyclidine|PCP]] for the first and only time, causing a "deep scar on his psyche". This changed his life overnight. He said he became an introvert, experienced anxiety and depression, dealing with this period for over two years.<ref name="Reiff2020">{{cite book|author=Corbin Reiff|title=Total F*cking Godhead: The Biography of Chris Cornell|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PpjuDwAAQBAJ&pg=PT17|date=July 28, 2020|publisher=Post Hill Press|isbn=978-1-64293-216-4|page=17}}</ref>

[[File:Chris Cornell Posters.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Chris Cornell posters in Los Angeles (2018)]]

On July 11, 2017, the [[Detroit Police Department]]<ref name="report details">{{cite web|title=Reports add details about Cornell's death|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/detroit-city/2017/07/11/cornell-death-details/103609948/|website=The Detroit News|access-date=July 28, 2017|date=July 11, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729092248/http://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/detroit-city/2017/07/11/cornell-death-details/103609948/|archive-date=July 29, 2017}}</ref> released the full police report on Cornell's death,<ref name="full police report">{{cite web|url=http://content-static.detroitnews.com/pdf/2017/cornell.pdf|title=Chris Cornell Full Police Report from the Detroit Police Department|work=Detroit News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180222063858/http://content-static.detroitnews.com/pdf/2017/cornell.pdf|archive-date=February 22, 2018|access-date=March 4, 2018}}</ref> along with photographs from Cornell's hotel room<ref name="hotel room photos">{{cite web |url=https://www.tmz.com/2017/07/11/chris-cornell-death-police-release-hotel-room-photos/ |title=Chris Cornell's Death, Police Release Hotel Room Photos |work=TMZ |date=July 11, 2017 |access-date=July 12, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170713012024/http://www.tmz.com/2017/07/11/chris-cornell-death-police-release-hotel-room-photos/ |archive-date=July 13, 2017 }}</ref> and the 911 call from the MGM Grand Detroit from the night of Cornell's death.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://loudwire.com/911-call-documents-night-chris-cornell-death-released/ |title=911 Call and Documents From Night of Chris Cornell's Death Released |work=Loudwire |date=July 11, 2017 |access-date=July 12, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170712073342/http://loudwire.com/911-call-documents-night-chris-cornell-death-released/ |archive-date=July 12, 2017 }}</ref> The call was made by a hotel employee at 12:56&nbsp;a.m., reporting "a nonresponsive guest... inside of Room 1136."<ref name="full report">{{cite web|title=Full account of Soundgarden singer Chris Cornell's death emerges|url=http://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/detroit/2017/07/11/chris-cornell-death-detroit-final-police-report/467990001/|website=Detroit Free Press|access-date=July 28, 2017|date=July 11, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170730022731/http://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/detroit/2017/07/11/chris-cornell-death-detroit-final-police-report/467990001/|archive-date=July 30, 2017}}</ref> According to the report, Martin Kirsten (Cornell's bodyguard) was at the singer's hotel room at 11:30&nbsp;p.m. to help him with his computer. It also says that Cornell's wife, Vicky, talked to her husband at 11:35&nbsp;p.m. Alarmed by what she heard, Vicky phoned Kirsten at 12:15&nbsp;am to ask him to check on her husband "because he did not sound like he was OK."<ref name="TDN">{{cite web|title=Chris Cornell death probe leaves some unsatisfied|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/detroit-city/2017/07/10/chris-cornell-death-fan-questions-unanswered/103567836/|website=The Detroit News|access-date=July 28, 2017|date=July 10, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728131622/http://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/detroit-city/2017/07/10/chris-cornell-death-fan-questions-unanswered/103567836/|archive-date=July 28, 2017}}</ref> According to Vicky, Cornell kept saying, "I am just tired," and hung up the phone.<ref name="full police report"/> The call prompted Kirsten to go to Cornell's suite to check on him.<ref name="full police report"/> Unable to enter the room because of the interior latch, Kirsten returned to his room and called hotel security. Security refused to assist.<ref name="report details"/>

Kirsten told police that he went to Cornell's room at around 12:15&nbsp;a.m., but could not access the locked room. He then had a telephone conversation with Vicky, who instructed him to kick the door open, as the hotel staff refused to do it. Kirsten told police in a signed statement that he kicked the bedroom door 6–7 times before it opened, then went inside, and the bathroom door was partially opened and he could see Cornell's feet.<ref name="full police report"/> Kirsten said that Vicky was on the phone with him the whole time asking for updates.<ref name="report details"/> Kirsten said in his statement that he loosened the band around Cornell's neck, then tried to resuscitate him by compressing his chest.<ref name="full police report"/> Medical personnel arrived at 12:56&nbsp;a.m. and tried to resuscitate Cornell, with no success.<ref name="TDN"/><ref name="report details"/> Cornell was pronounced dead at around 1:30&nbsp;a.m.,<ref name="report details"/> an hour and 15 minutes after his bodyguard was first contacted by Cornell's wife.<ref name="full police report"/>

Questioned by ''[[The Detroit News]]'' why it took 41 minutes to get a medical team to the scene after the bodyguard found Cornell lying on the floor, police insisted that there were no gaps.<ref name="TDN"/> Investigators looked at the length of the phone call between Cornell and his wife, and the calls the bodyguard made to security and checked video surveillance footage from the hotel hallway, and determined the timeline was accurate, and the bodyguard's story was accurate.<ref name="TDN"/> On May 15, 2018, Vicky Cornell told ''The Detroit News'' that she was dissatisfied with the autopsy report, stating it was incomplete and giving rise to conspiracy theorists of which she and her family were victims. She pointed out that her husband also suffered from a head injury mentioned in two clinical reports that did not appear in the autopsy report.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://eu.detroitnews.com/story/entertainment/people/2018/05/15/chris-cornell-widow-rips-probe-detroit-death/34918321/ |title=Chris Cornell widow rips probe year after Detroit death |last=Hunter |first=George |date=May 15, 2018 |newspaper=The Detroit News}}</ref>

On November 1, 2018, Vicky Cornell and her children filed suit in Los Angeles Superior Court, claiming that Dr. Robert Koblin "negligently and repeatedly" prescribed "dangerous mind-altering controlled substances to Chris Cornell which impaired Mr. Cornell's cognition, clouded his judgment, and caused him to engage in dangerous impulsive behaviors that he was unable to control, costing him his life."<ref name=Dalton>{{cite news|url=https://www.journalnow.com/news/nation_world/family-of-singer-chris-cornell-sues-doctor-over-his-death/article_daeb320d-ab4c-5ff7-97b1-84326da50a91.html|title=Family of singer Chris Cornell sues doctor over his death |last=Dalton|first=Andrew|work=[[Winston-Salem Journal]]|agency=Associated Press|date=November 1, 2018|access-date=November 2, 2018}}</ref> The suit claims Koblin prescribed lorazepam over a period of 20 months without seeing Cornell.<ref name=Dalton/> In his motion for dismissal, Koblin denied all accusations of negligence and said that Cornell was well aware of the risks inherent to the medication, which he was taking to treat anxiety. Koblin ordered Cornell the first prescription of lorazepam in September 2015. Koblin insisted that he did everything within his power to help Cornell, and that a malpractice law should shield him from being sued.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.legalreader.com/doctor-chris-cornell-negligence-lawsuit/ |title=Doctor for Late Soundgarden Singer Chris Cornell Moves to Dismiss Negligence Lawsuit |last=J. Farrick |first=Ryan |date=March 5, 2019 |website=Legal Reader}}</ref> In April 2021, the two parties settled on a confidential agreement.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/chris-cornell-family-settlement-doctor-1166269/ |title=Chris Cornell's Family Settles With Doctor Who Prescribed Singer Drugs |last=Kreps |first=Daniel |date=May 6, 2021 |website=Rollingstone}}</ref>

===Memorial and tributes===
[[File:Chris Cornell Grave.jpg|thumb|Cornell's grave at the Hollywood Forever Cemetery]]

Cornell's body was cremated on May 23, 2017.<ref name=cremated>{{cite web |url=http://loudwire.com/chris-cornell-cremated-ahead-of-friday-funeral/ |title=Chris Cornell Cremated Ahead of Friday's Funeral |work=Loudwire |date=May 24, 2017 |access-date=May 24, 2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170524172733/http://loudwire.com/chris-cornell-cremated-ahead-of-friday-funeral/ |archive-date=May 24, 2017 }}</ref> His funeral took place on May 26, 2017, at the [[Hollywood Forever Cemetery]] in Los Angeles.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/may/26/chris-cornell-memorial-service-soundgarden-hollywood-cemetery|title=Mourners and fans gather for Chris Cornell's memorial service|agency=Associated Press|date=May 26, 2017|work=The Guardian|access-date=May 27, 27, 2017}}</ref> Attendees and speakers at the ceremony included Soundgarden members [[Kim Thayil]], [[Matt Cameron]], and [[Ben Shepherd]], as well as former members [[Hiro Yamamoto]] and [[Scott Sundquist]], along with Audioslave's [[Tom Morello]], and Pearl Jam/Temple of the Dog members [[Jeff Ament]] and [[Mike McCready]].<ref>{{YouTube|id=S3bpwaR3gak|title=Mike McCready Talks About Chris Cornell and his Friendship with Eddie Vedder}}</ref> The mourners included friends and families as well as many notable musicians<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nbclosangeles.com/multimedia/Raw-Video-Chris-Cornell-Memorial-Service_Los-Angeles-424682604.html |title=Raw Video: Chris Cornell Memorial Service |date=May 26, 2017 |website=NBC Los Angeles |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170531221428/http://www.nbclosangeles.com/multimedia/Raw-Video-Chris-Cornell-Memorial-Service_Los-Angeles-424682604.html |archive-date=May 31, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/Rock-Royalty-Pay-Final-Respects-at-Chris-Cornell-Funeral-424664824.html |title=Chris Cornell Funeral: A-Listers, Rock Royalty Pay Final Respects |date=May 26, 2017 |website=NBC Los Angeles |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170816211932/http://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/Rock-Royalty-Pay-Final-Respects-at-Chris-Cornell-Funeral-424664824.html |archive-date=August 16, 2017}}</ref> and others.<ref name="funeral">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/chris-cornell-laid-to-rest-at-private-los-angeles-funeral-w484613|title=Chris Cornell Laid to The ceremony began with the cemetery's speakers playing Audioslave's "Like a Stone", as well as Cornell's last solo song released before his death, "The Promise". [[Linkin Park]]'s [[Chester Bennington]] and [[Brad Delson]] performed [[Leonard Cohen]]'s [[Hallelujah (Leonard Cohen song)|"Hallelujah"]]. At the end of the funeral, Temple of the Dog's song "All Night Thing" accompanied mourners as they exited.<ref name="funeral"/> Cornell's ashes were placed next to a [[cenotaph]] statue for his friend [[Johnny Ramone]]<ref name="funeral"/> – Ramone's ashes were retained by his widow.<ref>{{cite news |title=Johnny Ramone immortalized in bronze |newspaper=USA Today |date=January 7, 2005 |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/life/people/2005-01-07-ramone-statue_x.htm |access-date=July 29, 2017}}</ref>

Seattle's [[Space Needle]] observation tower went dark from 9:00&nbsp;p.m. to 10:00&nbsp;p.m. PST on May 18, 2017, in honor of Cornell and his contributions to the city's music scene.<ref>{{cite 2017}}</ref> [[Oakland Athletics]] player [[Trevor Plouffe]] changed his walk-up music to "Black Hole Sun" to honor Cornell.<ref>{{cite 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170701113435/http://ftw.usatoday.com/2017/05/trevor-plouffe-mariners-chris-cornell|archive-date=July 1, 2017}}</ref> [[Linkin Park]] dedicated their performance of "[[One More Light (song)|One More Light]]" on ''[[Jimmy Kimmel Live!]]'' in tribute to Cornell.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/linkin-park-one-more-light-jimmy-kimmel-live-chris-cornell/|title=Linkin Park Dedicate 'One More Light' Performance on 'Jimmy Kimmel Live' to Chris Cornell|work=Loudwire|date=May 19, 2017|access-date=July 27, the 2017 [[Billboard Music Awards]], [[Imagine Dragons]]' lead singer, [[Dan Reynolds (musician)|Dan Reynolds]], paid tribute to Cornell remembering his life and career and asking for a moment of silence as a photo of Cornell filled television screens at home and the monitors in the venue.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/bbma/7801230/chris-cornell-imagine-dragons-billboard-music-awards-tribute-2017|title=Imagine Dragons' Dan Reynolds Pays Tribute to Chris Cornell at
