'''Buckcherry''' is an American [[hard rock]] band from [[Anaheim, California]], formed in 1995. The band released two albums, ''[[Buckcherry (album)|Buckcherry]]'' (1999) and ''[[Time Bomb (Buckcherry album)|Time Bomb]]'' (2001), before dissolving in 2002. Buckcherry's first album ''Buckcherry'' was DreamWorks' first album to go gold. In 2005, lead vocalist [[Josh Todd (musician)|Josh Todd]] and lead guitarist Keith Nelson reformed Buckcherry with a new lineup and released a new album in 2006, ''[[15 (Buckcherry album)|15]]''. It contained Buckcherry's biggest crossover hits to date, "[[Crazy Bitch]]", and their first [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] top ten hit, "[[Sorry (Buckcherry song)|Sorry]]". The band continued to record albums, releasing seven between 2008 and 2023: ''[[Black Butterfly (Buckcherry album)|Black Butterfly]]'' in 2008, ''[[All Night Long (Buckcherry album)|All Night Long]]'' in 2010, ''[[Confessions (Buckcherry album)|Confessions]]'' in 2013, ''[[Rock 'n' Roll (Buckcherry album)|Rock 'n' Roll]]'' in 2015, ''[[Warpaint (Buckcherry album)|Warpaint]]'' in 2019, ''Hellbound'' in 2021 and ''Vol. 10'' in 2023. Their eleventh album, ''[[Roar Like Thunder]]'' was released in June 2025.

==History==

===Formation: 1995–1999===
[[Josh Todd (musician)|Josh Todd]] grew up in the [[Anaheim Hills]] neighborhood of [[Anaheim, California]] and later moved to [[Lake Forest, California]]. Early on, Todd fronted the Hollywood glam rock band Slamhound. He eventually met lead guitarist Keith Nelson through their tattoo artist (Kevin Quinn).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://tattoo.about.com/od/newsandviews/a/Interview-With-Buckcherry-Josh-Todd-And-Xavier-Muriel-Talk-Tattoos.htm |title=Tattoos of Buckcherry - Buckcherry Rock Band Interview - Josh Todd and Xavier Muriel's Tattoos |publisher=Tattoo.about.com |date=August 3, 2010 |access-date=February 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130403113404/http://tattoo.about.com/od/newsandviews/a/Interview-With-Buckcherry-Josh-Todd-And-Xavier-Muriel-Talk-Tattoos.htm |archive-date=April 3, 2013 |url-status=dead  }}</ref> The duo made a few demos before being joined by bassist [[Jonathan Brightman]] and drummer Devon Glenn, calling themselves Sparrow. Sparrow began performing around the Hollywood club scene, receiving a strong, local following due to their old school [[rock and roll]] vibe, and were signed to [[DreamWorks Records]] shortly after. The group changed its name to Buckcherry after receiving a cease-and-desist letter from a record label called [[Sparrow Records|Sparrow]] (owned by [[EMI]]). Although the band's name is a [[spoonerism]] of the late [[Chuck Berry]], the group said it was inspired by a drag queen acquaintance of theirs named Buck Cherry.

===Commercial success: 1999–2002===
The band released its [[Buckcherry (album)|self-titled debut]] in 1999 to critical praise and certified gold sales. The album, produced by [[Terry Date]] ([[Soundgarden]]/[[Mother Love Bone]]/[[Pantera]]/[[Steve Jones (musician)|Steve Jones]]/[[Deftones]]), included the hit singles "[[Lit Up]]", "[[For the Movies]]", "[[Dead Again (song)|Dead Again]]", and "[[Check Your Head (song)|Check Your Head]]".

After adding rhythm guitarist Yogi Lonich to the lineup in 1999, Buckcherry toured nonstop in support of the debut album, including opening for [[Lenny Kravitz]] on his Freedom Tour (1999) and participating at the infamous [[Woodstock 99]], before going back into the studio in 2000 to work on a follow-up, ''[[Time Bomb (Buckcherry album)|Time Bomb]]'' (2001). The second album was considered a disappointment by many critics,<ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite web|last=Jacobetz |first=Steven |url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/time-bomb-mw0000586701 |title=Time Bomb - Buckcherry : Songs, Reviews, Credits, Awards |publisher=AllMusic |date=March 27, 2001 |access-date=February 22, 2013}}</ref> and it did not fare as well on the charts. [[Allmusic]] noted that "For a second record, it's surprising how jaded and [[nihilism|nihilistic]] they are already."<ref name=autogenerated1 />
Buckcherry performed opening dates for [[AC/DC]] in the spring of 2000.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.allaccessmagazine.com/vol5/issue03/buckcherry.html |title=Buckcherry :: Fifteen :: All Access Magazine :: It's All About The Music |publisher=All Access Magazine |date=March 15, 2007 |access-date=February 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719143553/http://www.allaccessmagazine.com/vol5/issue03/buckcherry.html |archive-date=July 19, 2011 |url-status=usurped }}</ref> From August 2001 through January 2002, as tension over the musical direction set in, [[Jonathan Brightman]], Yogi Lonich, and Devon Glenn each successively left Buckcherry, and were replaced by Dave Markasky, Josh Fleeger, and Matt Lawrence, respectively. Josh Todd and Keith Nelson still planned to continue the band, and began the writing process for a third album. The album was never completed, however, and the band was put on hiatus in July 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/music/artist/buckcherry/artist.jhtml#bio |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120524153159/http://www.mtv.com/music/artist/buckcherry/artist.jhtml%23bio |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 24, 2012 |title=Buckcherry &#124; New Music And Songs |publisher=MTV |access-date=February 22, 2013}}</ref>

===Other projects: 2002–2005===
[[Josh Todd (musician)|Josh Todd]] and Keith Nelson performed together along with ex-[[Guns N' Roses]] members [[Slash (musician)|Slash]], [[Duff McKagan]], and [[Matt Sorum]] (also of [[The Cult]]) at the [[Randy Castillo]] tribute concert. Speculation ensued that Josh Todd would become the lead vocalist of the project headed up by Slash, Duff McKagan, and Matt Sorum. Josh Todd spent a month in the studio, reportedly completing 10 songs, but was abruptly dropped from the project by Slash. Todd was quoted as saying, "It was amazing, the band was slamming, and then Slash just came in one day and just shit-canned the whole thing". In his autobiography, Slash says the reason was because he was displeased with how Todd's voice sounded when they played the material back. [[Scott Weiland]] of [[Stone Temple Pilots]] was eventually chosen to helm the band that would become known as [[Velvet Revolver]]. Keith Nelson was given a songwriting credit on Velvet Revolver's track "[[Dirty Little Thing]]". Nelson then went on to write and produce on various records.

===Commercial success and ''Crüe Fest'': 2005–2009===
[[File:Buckcherry B&W.jpg|thumb|upright=1.2|Buckcherry at the Sunshine Theater in 2007]]
In 2005, Josh Todd reformed Buckcherry with Keith Nelson and new members Stevie D. of [[Automatic Black]], Jimmy Ashhurst, and Xavier Muriel.
In 2006, the band released the album ''[[15 (Buckcherry album)|15]]'' to commercial and critical success. It resurrected the band with hits "[[Crazy Bitch]]", "[[Sorry (Buckcherry song)|Sorry]]", "[[Everything (Buckcherry song)|Everything]]" and "Next 2 You".

Back on September 11, 2006, another lawsuit had been filed against the band, their current record label, and other related companies on behalf of a sixteen-year-old girl who claimed she was coerced into appearing topless and in various sexual scenarios at a concert while the band was playing a sexually related song. According to sources, however, all participants in the [[Crazy Bitch]] video<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/general_music_news/buckcherry_sued_over_crazy_bitch_video.html | title=Buckcherry Sued over 'Crazy Bitch' Video }}</ref> had to show proof that they were over eighteen years old and sign a release form further reaffirming their age. Band attorney Skip Miller is quoted in several news stories as stating, "This woman filled out a release form with false information. And once it was determined this woman was underage, the video was removed."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2006-sep-11-fi-warner11-story.html|title=Labels Sued Over Sexy Video of Minor|last=Duhigg|first=Charles|date=September 11, 2006|website=L.A. Times|access-date=February 28, 2018}}</ref>

On April 15, 2008, Buckcherry announced they would be touring as part of [[Mötley Crüe]]'s ''[[Crüe Fest]]'', along with [[Papa Roach]], [[Sixx:A.M.]], and [[Trapt]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.musicgeekmedia.com/?p=19#more-19 |title=Musicgeekmedia.com |publisher=Musicgeekmedia.com |access-date=February 22, 2013 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090805085620/http://www.musicgeekmedia.com/?p=19#more-19 |archive-date=August 5, 2009 }}</ref> The tour began July 1, 2008, in [[West Palm Beach, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stltoday.com/blogzone/the-blender/the-blender/2008/04/concert-announcement-cruefest-with-motley-crue/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20090623014330/http://www.stltoday.com/blogzone/the-blender/the-blender/2008/04/concert-announcement-cruefest-with-motley-crue/|url-status=dead|title=Concert Announcement: Cruefest with Motley Crue &#124; The Blender &#124; STLtoday|archive-date=June 23, 2009|access-date=April 17, 2008}}</ref>

On September 16, 2008, the band released their fourth album, ''[[Black Butterfly (Buckcherry album)|Black Butterfly]]'', which debuted at number 8 on the top 200 charts. It was the number one rock album that week. That year, [[Josh Todd (musician)|Josh Todd]] was featured on the album ''[[This War Is Ours]]'' by [[Escape the Fate]]. He sang co-lead vocals in the song "[[10 Miles Wide]]" and backing vocals on "Harder Than You Know". In 2009, he was featured in the music video for "10 Miles Wide".

In May 2009, [[Kiss (band)|KISS]] announced that Buckcherry would be the opening band in their 2009/10 US and Canadian tour. On July 30, Buckcherry was featured in the Kerrang! Week Of Rock Tour with [[The 69 Eyes]] and Hardcore Superstar at the HMV Forum in London. Other bands in the Week Of Rock included [[Limp Bizkit]], [[Youmeatsix]], and [[Lacuna Coil]]. [[DragonForce]] was also supposed to play during the Week Of Rock, but pulled out.

On September 29, 2009, Buckcherry released their first live album, ''[[Live & Loud 2009]]'', which they played some of their biggest songs such as "[[Sorry (Buckcherry song)|Sorry]]", "[[Lit Up]]", "[[Crazy Bitch]]", and much more. The album was recorded in May 2009 during their Canadian tour in [[Edmonton]], [[Calgary]], [[Medicine Hat]], and [[Regina, Saskatchewan|Regina]].

===''All Night Long'' and ''Confessions'': 2010–2013===
It was announced on February 22, 2010, that Buckcherry would be a part of Rocklahoma 2010 in [[Pryor, Oklahoma]].

Bassist Jimmy Ashhurst is one of the characters in the book ''Sex Tips from Rock Stars'' by Paul Miles, published by [[Omnibus Press]] in July 2010.<ref>{{cite web|author=Paul Miles |url=http://sextipsfromrockstars.com |title=Sex Tips From Rock Stars by Paul Miles |publisher=Sextipsfromrockstars.com |access-date=February 22, 2013}}</ref>

Buckcherry released their fifth studio album, titled ''[[All Night Long (Buckcherry album)|All Night Long]]'', on August 3, 2010.<ref>[http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/Blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=139990 Blabbermouth.net - Buckcherry: New Album Release Date Confirmed] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100516204033/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=139990 |date=May 16, 2010 }}. Retrieved June 6, 2010.</ref> The album was mixed by [[Mike Fraser (record producer)|Mike Fraser]]. The first single from the album, "[[All Night Long (Buckcherry song)|All Night Long]]", was originally going to be released to rock radio on May 3, but was pushed back to May 24.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fmqb.com/article.asp?id=16697 |title=Radio Industry News, Music Industry Updates, Arbitron Ratings, Music News and more! |publisher=FMQB |access-date=February 22, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110926075958/http://www.fmqb.com/Article.asp?id=16697 |archive-date=September 26, 2011 }}</ref> It was released as a free download to all fans who posted a pre-defined "tweet" on [[Twitter]] or a similar message on [[Facebook]] on May 4. The album debuted at No.&nbsp;10 on the Billboard Top 200 Album chart and was the No.&nbsp;1 Rock debut.

The band released the holiday themed single "Christmas is Here" as a digital download on November 30, 2010.

From January 19 to March 18, 2011, Buckcherry toured with [[Hellyeah]] and [[All That Remains (band)|All That Remains]] on the Jägermeister Music Tour.

As of June 2011, according to Keith Nelson, the band were already writing new material for their next album.<ref>{{cite web|title=BUCKCHERRY Continuing Work On New Material|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=159624|website=Blabbermouth.net|date = June 19, 2011|access-date=June 19, 2011}}</ref>

The band contributed the song, "Wherever I Go," for the ''Avengers Assemble'' soundtrack.<ref>{{cite web|title=Soundgarden records new song for Avengers movie|url=http://marvel.com/news/movies/18392/soundgarden_records_new_song_for_avengers_movie|date=March 27, 2012|publisher=Marvel.com|access-date=March 12, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150325184906/http://marvel.com/news/movies/18392/soundgarden_records_new_song_for_avengers_movie|archive-date=March 25, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Buckcherry's sixth album, ''[[Confessions (Buckcherry album)|Confessions]]'', was released February 19, 2013.<ref name=gluttonyloudwire>{{cite web|last=Childers|first=Chad|title=Buckcherry Unleash New Single 'Gluttony' Off Upcoming Album 'Confessions'|url=http://loudwire.com/buckcherry-unleash-new-single-gluttony-off-upcoming-album-confessions/|work=Loudwire|date=December 7, 2012 |access-date=December 8, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Confessions|url=https://www.amazon.com/Confessions-Buckcherry/dp/B00AJLHUGM/ref=sr_1_2?ie=UTF8&qid=1354987211&sr=8-2&keywords=buckcherry+confessions|work=Amazon.com|access-date=December 8, 2012}}</ref> The first single from ''Confessions'', "Gluttony", was made available for streaming on December 7, 2012.<ref name=gluttonyloudwire />

=== ''Fuck EP'', ''Rock 'N' Roll'' and ''Warpaint'': 2014–2020 ===
[[File:Buckcherry Rock am Ring 2014 (24).JPG|upright=1.2|thumb|Buckcherry at [[Rock am Ring]] 2014]]
[[Fuck (EP)|''Fuck'']] was released on August 19, 2014. The title of every song on the EP includes the word "Fuck". The song, "Say Fuck It" is a cover of the 2012 [[Icona Pop]] song "[[I Love It (Icona Pop song)|I Love It]]", with a few modifications in the lyrics.

Buckcherry took part in VampPark Fest on February 19, 2015, hosted by the rock band [[Vamps (band)|Vamps]] at the [[Nippon Budokan]].<ref>{{cite web| title=VAMPS to hold VAMPARK FEST rock festival at Budokan| url=http://www.en.barks.jp/news/?id=1000005212| work=barks.jp| access-date=February 7, 2015| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170703134629/http://www.en.barks.jp/news/?id=1000005212| archive-date=July 3, 2017| url-status=dead}}</ref>

Buckcherry's seventh studio album ''[[Rock 'n' Roll (Buckcherry album)|Rock 'n' Roll]]'' was released on August 21, 2015. On June 2, 2015, "Bring It On Back" was released as the first single from the album. A second single, "The Feeling Never Dies," which features country singer [[Gretchen Wilson]], was released February 17, 2016.

In May 2017, Keith Nelson and Xavier Muriel left the band due to disagreements with Josh Todd over the band's direction. The band was said by [[Eddie Trunk]] and former bassist Jimmy Ashhurst to have over-toured. This was one of many reasons Keith and Xavier left the band. However Keith and Xavier have both stated they have no hard feelings. The band brought in new members guitarist Kevin Roentgen and drummer Sean Winchester shortly afterwards. Nelson's departure left Josh Todd as the only remaining original member of Buckcherry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chadwick |first=Robert |date=June 24, 2023 |title=RECAP & PHOTOS: Buckcherry Live at The Corral |url=http://www.govenuemagazine.com/recap-photos-buckcherry-live-at-the-corral/ |access-date=December 5, 2023 |website=Go Venue Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

The band's eighth studio album ''[[Warpaint (Buckcherry album)|Warpaint]]'' was released in 2019. The title track was released on February 8, 2019, and the full album on March 8, 2019.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/business/8501595/josh-todd-talks-new-buckcherry-album-warpaint-reflects-on-20-years|title=Buckcherry's Josh Todd on New 'Warpaint' Album & 20 Years as a Band: 'That's Really What I Visualized'|magazine=Billboard}}</ref>

Guitarist Kevin Roentgen left the band in July 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/buckcherry-guitarist-kevin-roentgen-quits/|title=BUCKCHERRY Guitarist KEVIN ROENTGEN Quits|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=August 23, 2020}}</ref> He was later replaced by [[Jetboy (band)|Jetboy]] guitarist Billy Rowe.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/buckcherry-recruits-jetboy-guitarist-billy-rowe/|title=BUCKCHERRY Recruits JETBOY Guitarist BILLY ROWE|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=August 27, 2020}}</ref>

In October 2020, it was reported that Buckcherry were due to enter the studio to record a new album.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|date=October 14, 2020|title=BUCKCHERRY To Enter Studio In Late October To Record 'Great' New Album|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/buckcherry-to-enter-studio-in-late-october-to-record-great-new-album/|access-date=December 10, 2020}}</ref>

=== ''Hellbound'', ''Vol. 10'' and ''Roar Like Thunder'': 2021–present ===
On April 21, 2021, Buckcherry announced their ninth album ''Hellbound'' (released on June 25, 2021, through [[Earache Records]] and Round Hill Records), along with the release of the single "So Hott" and its accompanying video (which was nominated for ''Classic Rock'' magazine's Track Of The Week<ref>{{Cite web|date=April 26, 2021|title=Tracks of the Week: new music from Yola, Mammoth WVH, Buckcherry and more|url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/tracks-of-the-week-new-music-from-yola-mammoth-wvh-buckcherry-and-more|url-status=live|access-date=April 27, 2021|website=[[Louder Sound]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426032946/https://www.loudersound.com/features/tracks-of-the-week-new-music-from-yola-mammoth-wvh-buckcherry-and-more |archive-date=April 26, 2021 }}</ref>) and the announcement of a North American tour with dates from June 2021 - November 2021.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=April 21, 2021|title=BUCKCHERRY To Release 'Hellbound' Album In June; |archive-date=April 21, 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Divita|first=Joe|title=Buckcherry Drop 'So Hott' Video + Announce New Album 'Hellbound' + Huge Tour|url=https://loudwire.com/buckcherry-so-hott-song-lyrics-hellbound-album/|url-status=live|access-date=April 23, 2021|website=[[Loudwire]]|date=April 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421122614/https://loudwire.com/buckcherry-so-hott-song-lyrics-hellbound-album/ |archive-date=April 21, 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite In November 2024, it was announced that the band had entered the studio in [[Nashville]] with producer [[Marti Frederiksen]] to record their eleventh album.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/buckcherry-begins-recording-eleventh-studio-album | title=BUCKCHERRY Begins Recording Eleventh Studio Album|website=Blabbermouth.net | date=November 5, 2024 }}</ref>

The band's eleventh studio album, ''[[Roar Like Thunder]]'', was released on June 13, 2025. The album was preceded by the title track and "Come On" as the first two singles.
