|archive-date=8 January 2012 |access-date=7 October 2023 |url-status=bot: unknown }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> They released a debut EP ''Strange Behaviour'' on 9 August 2011 via iTunes. On 26 March 2012 Jet announced their "discontinuation as a group," via their official website and Facebook:<ref name="Scatena" />
{{blockquote|"A Message to Our Fans: After many successful years of writing, recording and touring we wish to announce our discontinuation as a group. From the many pubs, theatres, stadiums and festivals all across the world it was the fans that made our amazing story possible and we wish to thank them all. Thank you, and goodnight."<ref name="Jet Gone">{{cite web | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120919225107/http://jettheband.com/news/67961 | url = http://jettheband.com/news/67961 | title = A Message to Our Fans | publisher = Jet Official Website | date = 26 March 2012 | archive-date = 19 September 2012 | access-date = 15 August 2014 }}</ref>}}

According to ''Infectious Magazine''{{'}}s Rachel Schuler, "Later it was stated that personal issues and arguments were the reason for the split."<ref name="Schuler" />

===Reformations and upcoming fourth album (2016–present)===
Jet members announced in September 2016 that they would reform in the following year and were due to open five shows for [[Bruce Springsteen]] and the [[E Street Band]] on the latter's "[[The River Tour 2016#Oceanic leg/Summer '17 tour|Summer '17]]" tour in February 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-just-totally-stoked-reunion-rumours-big-time/ |title=Jet Just Totally Stoked Those Reunion Rumours Big Time |first1=Emmy |last1=Mack |date=11 September 2016 |newspaper=Music Feeds |access-date=6 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161230002549/http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-just-totally-stoked-reunion-rumours-big-time/ |archive-date=30 December 2016 }}</ref><ref name="Williams">{{cite web |url=http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-frontman-nic-cester-release-debut-solo-album-2017/ |title=Jet Frontman Nic Cester to Release Debut Solo Album In 2017 |first1=Tom |last1=Williams |website=Music Feeds |date=22 February 2017 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20180421233609/http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-frontman-nic-cester-release-debut-solo-album-2017/ |archive-date=21 April 2018 |access-date=7 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In October 2016 they announced on social media that their first headline show in 6&nbsp;years was due at Sydney's [[Taronga Zoo]] also in February 2017.<ref name="Williams" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/jettheband/app/123966167614127/|title=Jet – Tour Dates {{!}} Facebook|website=www.facebook.com|access-date=2016-12-29}}</ref> For the performance they were joined on stage by Macklin on keyboards and the Wolfgramm Sisters on backing vocals.<ref name="Young">{{cite web |url=http://thebrag.com/jet-taronga-zoo/amp/index.html |title=Jet @ Taronga Zoo |first1=David James |last1=Young |website=The Brag |date=20 February 2017 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20190615055919/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/169055/20190615-0055/thebrag.com/jet-taronga-zoo/amp/index.html |archive-date=15 June 2019 |access-date=6 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The show subsequently sold out, so a second one was added.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.facebook.com/jettheband/posts/10154780372429704:0 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/facebook/33476194703/10154780372429704 |archive-date=2022-02-26 |url-access=limited |title=Jet – Sydney! WildHoney & Bloods will be joining us at... {{!}} Facebook |website=www.facebook.com |access-date=2016-12-29}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Jet had made their official live return at a one-off headlining show at Melbourne's Gasometer Hotel on 31 January 2017. They performed with Macklin and played a 23&nbsp;song set-list, which drew from all three of studio albums.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.setlist.fm/setlist/jet/2017/the-gasometer-hotel-melbourne-australia-4bf82b3e.html|title=Jet Concert Setlist at The Gasometer Hotel, Melbourne on January 31, 2017|publisher=Setlist.FM|date=31 January 2017|access-date=2 February 2017}}</ref>

While living in [[Italy]], Nic had been invited by Simone Cogo ({{abbr|p.k.a.|performer known as}} [[the Bloody Beetroots]] or DJ Bob Rifo) to collaborate on "My Name Is Thunder".<ref name="Cashmere 3" /> Once Nic's band mates were appraised they joined the project, which was issued as a single in July 2017.<ref name="Cashmere 3">{{cite web |url=http://www.noise11.com/news/jet-the-bloody-beetroots-release-my-name-is-thunder-20170710.html |title=Jet + the Bloody Beetroots Release 'My Name Is Thunder' |first1=Paul |last1=Cashmere |website=Noise11.com |date=10 July 2017 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20200909003852/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/178078/20200909-0000/www.noise11.com/news/jet-the-bloody-beetroots-release-my-name-is-thunder-20170710.html |archive-date=9 September 2020 |access-date=6 October 2023 |url-status=bot: unknown }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The track is the Australian rock group's first new song in seven&nbsp;years.<ref name="John">{{cite web |url=http://tonedeaf.com.au/jet-just-released-first-song-in-seven-years/amp/index.html |title=Jet Just Released Their First Song in 7 Years, and It's Definitely not What We Were Expecting |first1=Brandon |last1=John |website=[[Luke Girgis#Brag Media|Tone Deaf]] |date=7 July 2017 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20170724110203/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/152679/20170724-0850/tonedeaf.com.au/jet-just-released-first-song-in-seven-years/amp/index.html |archive-date=24 July 2017 |access-date=6 October 2023 |url-status=live }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> It also appeared on the Italian artist's album, ''The Great Electronic Swindle'' (October 2017), Rifo reflected, "we had different ideas on the mixing and from that, we came up with two versions. It's the best of both our worlds!"<ref name="Cashmere 3" /><ref name="John" />

In 2018 the quartet announced their 15th anniversary Australian national tour for ''Get Born'', with dates in Newcastle, Sydney, Canberra, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide and Melbourne. They issued their first live album ''Get Born: Live at the Forum'' in May to commemorate that tour.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Tom |title=Jet Announce 2018 'Get Re-Born' 15th Anniversary National Tour |url=http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-announce-2018-get-re-born-15th-anniversary-national-tour/ |website=Music Feeds |access-date=6 October 2023 |date=13 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231005010759/https://musicfeeds.com.au/news/jet-announce-2018-get-re-born-15th-anniversary-national-tour/ |archive-date=5 October 2023 }}</ref> They made a brief UK visit, playing in Manchester and London. They supported [[Jimmy Barnes]] alongside Eskimo Joe in 2019,<ref>{{cite web |title=Jimmy Barnes, Jet and Eskimo Joe to Tour the Country in 2019 |url=https://www.abc.net.au/doublej/music-reads/music-news/jimmy-barnes-jet-eskimo-joe-tour-2019/11137218 |date=22 May 2019 |publisher=[[Double J (radio station)|Double J]] ([[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]] (ABC)) |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref> and played their final show of their reunion at the By The C open-air concert in [[Coffs Harbour]] on 26 October 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jet Setlist at Park Beach Reserve, Coffs Harbour, Australia |url=https://www.setlist.fm/setlist/jet/2019/park-beach-reserve-coffs-harbour-australia-3b9d3874.html |website=Setlist.FM |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref>

Nic then resumed his solo career, releasing an album, ''The Skipping Girl'', in 2021. It was a companion to his first children's book of the same name.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rose |first1=Anna |title=Jet's Nic Cester to Release Children's Book and Accompanying Album, 'Skipping Girl' |url=https://www.nme.com/en_au/news/music/jets-nic-cester-to-release-childrens-book-and-accompanying-album-skipping-girl-3085860 |website=NME Australia |date=3 November 2021 |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref> Nic as a member of a supergroup [[the Jaded Hearts Club]] had issued ''You've Always Been Here'' in October 2020.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shutler |first1=Ali |title=The Jaded Hearts Club – ''You've Always Been Here'' Review: Well-intentioned but Often Unlistenable Dad-Rock |url=https://www.nme.com/en_au/reviews/album/the-jaded-hearts-club-youve-always-been-here-review-2767923 |website=NME |date=2 October 2020 |publisher=BandLab Technologies |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref> Wilson performed as a member of the Australian Rock Collective (or ARC), which included Kram, Powderfinger's [[Darren Middleton]] and Davey Lane. ARC perform tribute shows of classic albums, such as the Beatles' ''[[Let It Be (album)|Let It Be]]'' and Neil Young's ''[[Harvest (Neil Young album)|Harvest]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=de la Couer |first1=Sidonie Bird |title=ARC to pay homage to Neil Young and The Beatles at the Palais Theatre |url=https://beat.com.au/arc-to-pay-homage-to-neil-young-and-the-beatles-at-the-palais-theatre/ |website=Beat Magazine |date=27 April 2022 |access-date=20 June 2022}}</ref>

At the end of 2022 Nic was interviewed on a podcast and revealed Jet were in talks to reunite in the studio. "Next year is the 20 year anniversary of the release of the first Jet album. We're actually in discussions right now, sharing musical ideas for the first time with the idea of maybe trying to release some new material next year. This is just as of 3 weeks ago, so we'll see if it happens or not. It's looking good so far."<ref>{{cite web |title=Nachts Um Halb 1 – The Music Podcast in 3D Audio |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/nachts-um-halb-1-der-musikpodcast-in-3d-audio/id1622205718?i=1000589777875 |access-date=18 December 2022 }}</ref> In June 2023 the quartet officially announced their reunion and shared Australian tour dates for that September where they would perform ''Get Born'' in its entirety.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Varvaris |first1=Mary |title=Jet Announce 'Get In April 2024, Jet announced that after 15 years, they had started work on a new album, tentatively due for release in 2025. The band also announced a limited edition 7-inch vinyl record containing the new song "Hurry Hurry", which was released in May. A music video for "Hurry Hurry" was released in September 2024.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ETT36M7_zs8 |title=Jet - Hurry Hurry (Official Video) |date=2024-09-05 |last=Jet |access-date=2024-09-17 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

==Activism==
In 2007 Jet members joined a public campaign by [[People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals]] (PETA), which called for an end to [[Seal hunting#Canada|Canada's annual seal hunt]].<ref name="Eliezer">{{cite web |url=http://www.themusic.com.au/imm_display7f3d.html |title=Christie Eliezer's Music Business News |first1=Christie |last1=Eliezer |website=In Music & Media |date=22 May 2007 |via=National Library of Australia |archive-url=http://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20090218024857/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/10761/20090218-0018/www.themusic.com.au/imm_display7f3d.html |archive-date=18 February 2009 |access-date=6 October 2023 |url-status=bot: unknown }}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The petition was signed by some 150,000 names, which included fellow Australian musicians [[John Butler (musician)|John Butler]], members of [[Something for Kate]], [[Red Riders]] and the Vines.<ref name="Eliezer" />

===The Fred Hollows Foundation===
In May 2008, Jet released a video clip on [[YouTube]], which is tribute to the work of the late [[Fred Hollows]] and The Fred Hollows Foundation.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hollows.org |title=The Fred Hollows Foundation|website=Hollows.org}}</ref> Nic highlighted Hollow's work to restore sight to people blinded by [[cataract]]s in developing countries, which was ongoing 15&nbsp;years after his death. "Hollows was such a big figure in Australia and he had a huge impact, but he passed away when there was still work to do," Cester said in a statement. "This clip is a bit of a reminder, hopefully it encourages people to make a donation to keep [Hollow]'s work going."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=569559 |title=Jet Releasing Fred Hollows Tribute Clip (Nine-MSN) |publisher=News.ninemsn.com.au |access-date=2011-09-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090112091123/http://news.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=569559 |archive-date=2009-01-12}}</ref> The video tribute uses Jet's song "Shine On" along with images compiled by [[The Fred Hollows Foundation]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://optuszoo.news.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=569559 |title=Jet releasing Fred Hollows tribute clip (Nine-MSN) |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090112083805/http://optuszoo.news.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=569559 |archive-date=2009-01-12}}</ref>

'''Living Colour''' is an American [[rock music|rock]] band from New York City, formed in 1984.<ref>These sources refer to Living Colour as a rock band:
*{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kRWt3Tikj5QC&pg=PA5 |page=5 |title=Right to Rock: The Black Rock Coalition and the Cultural Politics of Race |last=Mahon |first=Maureen |publisher=Duke University Press |date=June 23, 2004 |isbn=9780822333173}}
*{{cite magazine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yCUEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA88 |page=88 |title=Electric Warriors |last=Caramanica |first=Jon |date=February 2002 |magazine=[[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]]}}
*{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1-pH4i3jXvAC&pg=PA663 |page=663 |title=All Music Guide to Rock |editor1=Vladimir Bogdanov|editor2=Chris Woodstra|editor3=Stephen Thomas Erlewine |publisher=Hal Leonard Corporation |date=2002 |isbn=9780879306533}}
*{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_NNmFiUnSmUC&pg=PA926 |page=926 |title=The Encyclopedia of Popular Music |last=Larkin |first=Colin |publisher=Omnibus Press |date=May 27, 2011 |isbn=9780857125958}}</ref> The band consists of guitarist [[Vernon Reid]], lead vocalist [[Corey Glover]], drummer [[Will Calhoun]] and bassist [[Doug Wimbish]] who replaced [[Muzz Skillings]] in 1992. Their music is influenced by [[heavy metal music|heavy metal]], [[funk]], [[jazz]], [[hip-hop]], [[punk rock|punk]], and [[alternative rock]]. The band's lyrics range from the personal to the political, including social commentary on [[racism in the United States]].

Living Colour has released six studio albums. The band rose to fame with their debut album ''[[Vivid (Living Colour album)|Vivid]]'' in 1988.<ref name="The Great Rock Discography">{{cite book
| first= Martin C.
| last= Strong
| year= 2000
| title= The Great Rock Discography
| edition= 5th
| publisher= Mojo Books
| location= Edinburgh
| pages= 580–581
| isbn= 1-84195-017-3}}</ref> Although they scored several hits, Living Colour is best known for their signature song "[[Cult of Personality (song)|Cult of Personality]]", which won a [[Grammy Award]] for [[Best Hard Rock Performance]] in 1990 and has been consistently used as the entrance theme for professional wrestler [[CM Punk]] since 2011.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last1=Wilkening |first1=Matthew |title=Why Living Colour's 'Cult of Personality' Is CM Punk's Theme Song |url=https://ultimateclassicrock.com/cm-punk-cult-of-personality/ |website=Ultimate Classic Rock |date=August 20, 2021 |access-date=13 April 2023}}</ref> They were named Best New Artist at the 1989 [[MTV Video Music Awards]], and won their second Grammy Award for their follow-up album ''[[Time's Up (Living Colour album)|Time's Up]]'' (1990). Their third album, ''[[Stain (album)|Stain]]'' (1993), was also well received by music critics. After disbanding in 1995,<ref name="The Great Rock Discography"/> Living Colour reunited in late 2000,<ref>{{cite web|title= Living Colour singer Corey Glover looks back on 25 years of 'Vivid'|author= Dustin Schoof|url= http://www.lehighvalleylive.com/music/index.ssf/2013/03/living_colour_singer_corey_glo.html|work= LehighValleyLive.com|date= March 29, 2013|url-status= live|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160304105959/http://www.lehighvalleylive.com/music/index.ssf/2013/03/living_colour_singer_corey_glo.html|archive-date= March 4, 2016}}</ref> and has since released three more studio albums: ''[[Collideøscope]]'' (2003), ''[[The Chair in the Doorway]]'' (2009) and ''[[Shade (Living Colour album)|Shade]]'' (2017). The band has been working on new material for the follow-up to ''Shade''.<ref name="newmaterial">{{cite news|url=https://spotlightreport.net/on-the-spot-2/interview-corey-glover-of-living-colour-talks-oz-tour|title=Interview: Corey Glover of Living Colour Talks Oz Tour|website=Spotlightreport.net|date=December 12, 2018|access-date=February 28, 2020}}</ref>

==History==
===Early years (1984–1986)===
British-born guitarist [[Vernon Reid]] had formed several bands in the years before forming Living Colour in New York in 1984, using the [[British spelling]] of "colour".<ref>{{cite web |last1=James |first1=Joseph |title=Cult of Personality: An interview with Will Calhoun (Living Colour) |url=https://willnotfade.com/2017/04/30/will-calhoun-living-colour-interview/ |website=Will Not Fade |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190616211504/https://willnotfade.com/2017/04/30/will-calhoun-living-colour-interview/ |archive-date=June 16, 2019 |date=April 30, 2017 |quote=Band founder Vernon Reid is English, so made a deliberate choice to spell 'colour' correctly with the 'U' included. But most Americans spell many words incorrectly out of ignorance. It's not much of an issue.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Burgess |first1=Mick |title=We chat to Corey Glover from Living Colour ahead of Newcastle Riverside gig |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/whats-on/music-nightlife-news/corey-glover-living-colour-interview-13670041 |work=[[ChronicleLive]] |date=September 25, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171109073550/http://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/whats-on/music-nightlife-news/corey-glover-living-colour-interview-13670041 |archive-date=November 9, 2017}}</ref> Reid assembled several bands under the name Vernon Reid's Living Colour from 1984 to 1986.<ref name="rs">{{cite magazine|title=Living Colour's Time Is Now|author=David Fricke|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/living-colours-time-is-now-19901101|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=November 1, 1990|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170912232142/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/living-colours-time-is-now-19901101|archive-date=September 12, 2017}}</ref>  Reid was well known on the downtown New York jazz scenes because of his tenure in [[Ronald Shannon Jackson]]'s Decoding Society.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fricke |first1=David |title=Back in Black |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/back-in-black-2-95063/ |publisher=Rolling Stone Magazine |access-date=20 May 2021 |date=24 Sep 1987}}</ref>

Early band members included bassists Alex Mosely, [[Jerome Harris]] and Carl James, drummers Greg Carter, [[Pheeroan akLaff]] and J. T. Lewis, keyboardist [[Geri Allen]], and vocalists D. K. Dyson and [[Mark Ledford]], with Reid occasionally singing lead vocals himself. The band's sound was vastly different from the songs later in their significant label recordings. Material from this period included instrumental jazz/funk workouts, politically pointed [[punk rock]] burners, experimental excursions via Reid's guitar synth, and an early version of the song "[[Funny Vibe]]", which was reworked for their debut album ''[[Vivid (Living Colour album)|Vivid]]''.

===Mainstream success (1986–1991)===
[[File:Living-colour-live1993.jpg|thumb|upright=1.3|Living Colour in 1993]]
In 1986 a stable lineup was formed, consisting of vocalist/actor [[Corey Glover]], guitarist [[Vernon Reid]], bassist [[Muzz Skillings]], and drummer [[Will Calhoun]].<ref name="The Great Rock Discography"/> After hiring managers Jim Grant and Roger Cramer, the band hired prodigy [[lighting designer]] Andy Elias in November 1986 to strengthen their live shows with explosive visual productions.<ref>Panebianco, Julie. "Living Colour Rock The Ritz." ''East Village Eye,'' December 1986, p 6.</ref> The band became experienced at touring and performed regular gigs at the club [[CBGB]]. Around this time, their career also benefited from [[Rolling Stones]] singer [[Mick Jagger|Mick Jagger's]] involvement. Jagger's interest in Living Colour was piqued when Vernon Reid auditioned for the album ''[[Primitive Cool]]''; Jagger then arranged to see them live at CBGBs. Jagger went on to produce two of their demos. His endorsement encouraged major record labels to renew their interest in Living Colour, resulting in a recording contract with Epic Records.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2013/10/24/living-colours-vernon-reid-on-the-bands-formation-mick-jagger-and-reaching-audiences-through-grand-theft-auto|title = Living Colour's Vernon Reid on the band's formation, Mick Jagger, and reaching audiences through "Grand Theft Auto"|website=Denverpost.com| date=October 24, 2013 }}</ref> Interviewed in 2018, Vernon Reid looked back on the deal as a bittersweet triumph; "We had to get the co-sign from a person who literally embodied what rock 'n' roll is, the fact that he had to come see us, and dig us, for us to get at the back of the line is crazy."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theringer.com/music/2018/5/3/17312688/living-colour-cult-of-personality-vivid-30-years-anniversary|title = How Living Colour Reignited Rock's "Cult of Personality"|website=Theringer.com|date = May 3, 2018}}</ref>

''[[Vivid (Living Colour album)|Vivid]]'', released on May 3, 1988, gathered sales momentum when, later that year, [[MTV]] began playing the [[music video|video]] for "[[Cult of Personality (song)|Cult of Personality]]". The album reached No. 6 on the U.S. [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] chart. On April 1, 1989, the band performed on [[NBC]]'s ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''. Four months later, the band gained further exposure as an opening act, along with [[Guns N' Roses]], for [[The Rolling Stones]]' [[Steel Wheels/Urban Jungle Tour]].

In 1990, the band's second album, ''[[Time's Up (Living Colour album)|Time's Up]]'', featured songs in a variety of musical contexts; [[jazz fusion]], punk rock, [[Delta blues]], hip hop (cameos by [[Queen Latifah]] and [[Doug E. Fresh]]), funk, thrash metal, [[Jive (genre)|jive]], and hints of [[electronica]] were all represented.<ref>{{cite web |title= Living Colour Time's Up |author= Greg Prato |url= http://www.allmusic.com/album/times-up-mw0000315449 |work= [[AllMusic]] |access-date= August 21, 2015 |url-status= live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150806185836/http://www.allmusic.com/album/times-up-mw0000315449 |archive-date= August 6, 2015 }}</ref> The album reached No. 13 on the ''Billboard'' 200,<ref name="The Great Rock Discography"/> and won a [[Grammy Award]] for Best Hard Rock Performance. Other guests included [[Maceo Parker]] and [[Little Richard]].<ref name="The Great Rock Discography"/> The title track was "inspired" by pioneer punk group [[Bad Brains]], Vernon Reid said in 2025 during a performance on [[NPR]]'s [[List of Tiny Desk Concerts|Tiny Desk Concerts]], with Corey Glover joking that "we stole it (the song) from them."<ref>{{cite web |title=Living Colour: Tiny Desk Concert |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bzAI4F_ks5s&list=RDbzAI4F_ks5s&start_radio=1 |website=[[YouTube]] |publisher=[[NPR]] |access-date=27 June 2025 |date=25 June 2025}}</ref>

In 1991, Living Colour joined the inaugural [[Lollapalooza]] tour, and released an EP of outtakes entitled ''[[Biscuits (EP)|Biscuits]]''.<ref name="The Great Rock Discography"/>

===Second lineup and breakup (1992–1995)===
In 1992, Skillings left the band and was replaced by [[Doug Wimbish]].<ref name="The Great Rock Discography"/> This new lineup released their third album, ''[[Stain (album)|Stain]]'', in March 1993. The album reached No. 26 in the U.S., a further drop since its debut.<ref name="The Great Rock Discography"/> Despite retaining their strong fan base, Living Colour disbanded in January 1995 after failing to settle on common musical goals during their fourth studio album sessions.<ref name="The Great Rock Discography"/> Four of these tracks were included on the compilation ''[[Pride (Living Colour album)|Pride]]''. Following the breakup, individual band members released a variety of solo efforts.

===Reunion and subsequent events (2000–present)===
Living Colour re-formed on December 21, 2000, at [[CBGB]] as a gig billed "Head>>Fake w/ special guests". Head>>Fake was the current [[drum and bass]] project headed by Calhoun and Wimbish. Glover was on the bill to sing a few songs, and Reid came on after three songs. The reunion was followed by the release of the band's fourth studio album, ''[[Collideøscope]]'', in 2003, their first album not to chart in the United States, although it was critically praised.<ref>{{cite web |title=Review: Living Colour Collideoscope|author= Davey Boy |url= https://www.sputnikmusic.com/review/29750/Living-Colour-Collideoscope/|work= Sputnikmusic |date=March 4, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Living Colour Collideoscope|author=Dave Mount|url=http://www.prefixmag.com/reviews/living-colour/collideoscope/13482/|work=Prefixmag|date=March 6, 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924124749/http://www.prefixmag.com/reviews/living-colour/collideoscope/13482/|archive-date=September 24, 2015}}</ref> In 2005, Sony Records released ''[[Live from CBGB's]]'', a live album recorded on December 19, 1989, as well as another [[compilation album|best-of compilation]], ''[[Everything Is Possible: The Very Best of Living Colour]]'', with songs from ''Vivid'' to ''Collideøscope''. On September 22, 2006, Skillings joined the band for the first time in fourteen years when they played at a private party that drummer [[Jack DeJohnette]] threw for his wife, Lydia. Wimbish could not come back from his base in London to play for the event, so Skillings agreed to take over for the special private event.

[[File:Living Colour - Live Madrid 2008.jpg|thumb|Corey Glover and Doug Wimbish (2008)]]
[[File:Living Colour, live, Belly Up Tavern, Solana Beach, CA, March 29, 2013.jpg|thumb|Living Colour, San Diego, California, March 2013]]
The band performed a week-long European Tour starting on December 12, 2006. In May 2007, the band released their first live DVD – ''[[On Stage At World Cafe Live]]''. On July 11, 2008, the band performed at the 1980s hard rock-themed [[Rocklahoma]] festival at [[Pryor, Oklahoma|Pryor]], Oklahoma. Once again, Skillings performed with them in August 2008 for a Black Rock Coalition [[Band of Gypsys]] tribute in Harlem. They performed "Them Changes" and "Power of Soul".

On October 25, 2008, MVD Audio and CBGB Records released ''CBGB OMFUG Masters: August 19, 2005 The Bowery Collection'', a soundboard collection of songs from the Save CBGB's benefit show. On November 25, 2008, Inakustik and MVD released ''The Paris Concert'', a [[DVD]] recorded at [[New Morning (club)|New Morning]], in Paris, France, during their 2007 European Tour. The band released their fifth studio album, ''[[The Chair in the Doorway]]'', on September 15, 2009, on Megaforce Records. The album sold approximately 2,800 copies in its first week and landed at No. 161 on the ''Billboard'' 200. This was the band's first album to chart since ''Stain'' in 1993. The band toured the world in support of the record.<ref>[http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/268175/living-colour-back-with-fifth-studio-album Living Colour Back With Fifth Studio Album] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130423122206/http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/268175/living-colour-back-with-fifth-studio-album |date=April 23, 2013 }} Billboard.com. Retrieved on July 8, 2009.</ref>

In 2013, Living Colour performed "Cult of Personality" live during CM Punk's entrance at [[WrestleMania]] [[WrestleMania 29|29]] for his match against [[The Undertaker]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mirmina |first1=Graham |title=WWE WrestleMania 33: 5 Most underrated musical performances in the event's history |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/wwe/wwe-wrestlemania-33-5-most-underrated-musical-performances-in-events-history |website=Sportskeeda.com |date=March 29, 2017 |access-date=13 April 2023}}</ref>

On July 2, 2014, Living Colour announced on their official website that they were putting the finishing touches on their upcoming sixth album ''[[Shade (Living Colour album)|Shade]]'', which was released on September 8, 2017.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/living-colour-to-release-shade-album-in-september-cover-artwork-unveiled/|title=LIVING COLOUR To Release 'Shade' Album In September; Cover Artwork Unveiled|website=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=May 12, 2017|access-date=May 14, 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170515024742/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/living-colour-to-release-shade-album-in-september-cover-artwork-unveiled/|archive-date=May 15, 2017}}</ref> "''Shade'' is the sound of a band coming to terms with its shadows and light, From the blue pulpit of Robert Johnson to the mean red streets of Brooklyn to the golden lure of Hollywood, ''Shade'' is the next chapter of a unique American journey," Reid stated on the official website. The album includes ten originals and three covers: [[Robert Johnson]]'s "Preachin' Blues", [[The Notorious B.I.G.]]'s "[[Who Shot Ya?]]" and [[Marvin Gaye]]'s "[[Inner City Blues (Make Me Wanna Holler)|Inner City Blues]]" available on CD, MP3, and vinyl.

On August 19, 2016, the band released a cover of The Notorious B.I.G.'s "Who Shot Ya?" from an upcoming EP entitled ''Mixtape'' which was released on September 9.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/living-colour-to-release-mixtape-featuring-reinvention-of-notorious-b-i-g-s-who-shot-ya/|title=LIVING COLOUR To Release 'Mixtape' Featuring Reinvention Of NOTORIOUS B.I.G.'s 'Who Shot Ya'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=August 19, 2016|access-date=August 22, 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160822041658/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/living-colour-to-release-mixtape-featuring-reinvention-of-notorious-b-i-g-s-who-shot-ya|archive-date=August 22, 2016}}</ref> It features appearances from Chuck D, Black Thought, Pharoahe Monch, Prodigal Sunn, and Kyle Mansa.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pitchfork.com/news/67631-living-colour-enlist-chuck-d-black-thought-more-for-notorious-big-who-shot-ya-remake-listen/|title=Living Colour Enlist Chuck D, Black Thought, More for Notorious B.I.G. "Who Shot Ya" Remake: Listen |website=Pitchfork.com|date=August 18, 2016|access-date=May 5, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171122102435/https://pitchfork.com/news/67631-living-colour-enlist-chuck-d-black-thought-more-for-notorious-big-who-shot-ya-remake-listen/|archive-date=November 22, 2017}}</ref> Also in 2016, the band performed "Cult of Personality" on [[The Howard Stern Show]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WJXHFNw3fSw|title=Living Colour "Cult of Personality" on the Stern Show (2016)|website=Youtube.com|date=May 1, 2021|access-date=August 15, 2023}}</ref>

By late 2018, Living Colour had begun working on new material for a possible EP or seventh studio album.<ref name="newmaterial"/> When asked about a month after the release of ''Shade'' if fans would have to wait another four years for the follow-up album, Reid replied, "Well I don't know about all that. It's intriguing to be back in this cycle."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.albumism.com/interviews/vernon-reid-of-living-colour-navigates-the-shadows-and-light|title=INTERVIEW: Living Colour's Vernon Reid Navigates the Shadows and Light|website=Albumism.com|date=October 25, 2017|access-date=February 28, 2020}}</ref>

On September 2, 2022 during a performance at [[Rock in Rio]] in [[Rio de Janeiro, Brazil]], guitarist [[Steve Vai]] joined Living Colour on stage for a rendition of "Cult of Personality."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K3yDyZrKOV4|title=Living Colour - Cult Of Personality w/ Steve Vai at Rock In Rio 2022|publisher=[[YouTube]]|access-date=August 20, 2023|date=September 15, 2022}}</ref>

The band announced on December 10, 2022 that they had entered the studio to begin recording their seventh studio album.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bravewords.com/news/living-colour-check-in-from-the-studio-video|title=LIVING COLOUR Check In From The Studio (Video)|magazine=[[Brave Words & Bloody Knuckles]]|access-date=December 14, 2022|date=December 10, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/general_music_news/living_colour_is_in_the_studio_album_could_be_out_in_2023.html|title=Living Colour Is in the Studio, Album Could Be Out in 2023|publisher=[[Ultimate Guitar]]|access-date=December 14, 2022|date=December 12, 2022}}</ref>

In 2023, the band embarked on a US tour with [[Extreme (band)|Extreme]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://extreme-band.com/extreme-announce-2023-u-s-tour-with-living-colour-reveal-two-new-songs/|title=Extreme Announce 2023 U.S. Tour With Living Colour, Reveal Two New Songs|website=Extreme-band.com|date=April 20, 2023|access-date=August 15, 2023}}</ref>

In 2025, Living Colour performed "Cult of Personality" live during CM Punk's entrance at [[WrestleMania 41]] for his main event match against [[Roman Reigns]] and [[Seth Rollins]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bachar |first=Zach |title=Living Colour Plays 'Cult of Personality' for CM Punk's WWE WrestleMania 41 Entrance |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25188332-living-colour-plays-cult-personality-cm-punks-wwe-wrestlemania-41-entrance |access-date=2025-04-20 |website=Bleacherreport.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Acclaim and legacy==
Living Colour was ranked No.&nbsp;70 on [[VH1]]'s ''100 Greatest Artists of Hard Rock''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLxm64mApR05CJVCePlmcUFluSZyiAvKZ8|title=VH1 100 Greatest Artists of Hard Rock – YouTube|website=YouTube|access-date=May 5, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170521004536/https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLxm64mApR05CJVCePlmcUFluSZyiAvKZ8|archive-date=May 21, 2017}}</ref>

"[[Cult of Personality (song)|Cult of Personality]]" was re-recorded for ''[[Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock]]'', with an updated solo, as the original masters could not be used.

In October 2006, "[[Love Rears Its Ugly Head]]" was ranked and voted 303 out of the 2006 songs featured in the [[Triple M]] Essential 2006 Countdown.

''[[Rolling Stone]]'' have called the band "[[funk metal]] pioneers."<ref name="RS Living Colour">Fricke, David (November 13, 2003). [https://web.archive.org/web/20090412062112/http://www.rollingstone.com/artists/livingcolour/albums/album/290616/review/6209668/collideoscope Living Colour: Collideoscope : Music Reviews : Rolling Stone]. Archived from [https://web.archive.org/web/20090311015938/http://www.rollingstone.com/artists/livingcolour/albums/album/290616/review/6209668/collideoscope the original] on April 12, 2009. Retrieved February 1, 2012.</ref>

In early 2009, [[WWE]] used "Cult of Personality" in the video promoting the induction of [[Stone Cold Steve Austin]] into its Hall of Fame. Outside of his use of it in professional wrestling.

In 2011, [[WWE]] wrestler [[CM Punk]] returned with [[Cult of Personality (song)|Cult of Personality]] as his theme song for his highly anticipated Summer of Punk run. Punk had used this song before when he used to perform for [[Ring of Honor]]. Upon joining WWE, he did not try to get the song as his theme because he believed that WWE will not get a song licensed for a mid-card wrestler. He used the song for his [[All Elite Wrestling|AEW]] run as well between 2021 and 2023. CM Punk also entered to the song for his debut [[mixed martial arts]] bout at [[UFC 203]] and subsequently at [[UFC 225]] for his fight versus Mike Jackson.

'''Chevelle''' is an American [[Rock music|rock]] band formed in [[Grayslake, Illinois]], in 1995. The band was originally composed of brothers [[Pete Loeffler]] (lead vocals and guitar) and Sam Loeffler (drums and percussion) with Matt Scott (bass and backing vocals). Scott was replaced with Sam and Pete's brother, Joe Loeffler, in 1996. When Joe left the band in 2005, Geno Lenardo filled in as touring bassist until he was replaced with Pete and Sam's brother-in-law, [[Dean Bernardini]]. Bernardini departed the band in 2019, and in 2021, Kemble Walters joined as a touring bassist.

The band's first studio album, ''[[Point No. 1|Point #1]]'', was released on small record label [[Squint Entertainment]]. Chevelle's second album, ''[[Wonder What's Next]]'' (2002), was certified double platinum by the [[RIAA]] after a debut at No.&nbsp;14 on the United States albums chart, [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]. ''[[This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)]]'' (2004), the band's third album, debuted at No.&nbsp;8 and has been certified platinum. Chevelle has since released seven more albums: ''[[Vena Sera]]'' (2007), ''[[Sci-Fi Crimes]]'' (2009), ''[[Hats Off to the Bull]]'' (2011), ''[[La Gárgola]]'' (2014), ''[[The North Corridor]]'' (2016), ''[[NIRATIAS]]'' (2021), and ''[[Bright as Blasphemy]]'' (2025). Other releases from Chevelle include two live albums, two DVDs, and two compilation albums. As of 2022, the band has sold over 6 million records.

== History ==

=== Formation, ''Point #1'', and ''Wonder What's Next'' (1995–2003) ===
{{Main|Point No.&nbsp;1|Wonder What's Next|l1 = Point #1}}

[[File:Chevelle logo (band).svg|thumb|Logo used since Wonder What's Next.]]
Chevelle formed in 1995 in [[Grayslake, Illinois]], when brothers [[Pete Loeffler]] and Sam Loeffler started learning to play music.<ref name="AMG">{{Cite web|first=Tracy|last=Frey|url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/chevelle-mn0000091549/biography|title=Chevelle Biography - AllMusic|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=February 17, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013149/https://www.allmusic.com/artist/chevelle-mn0000091549/biography|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="crossrhythms">{{cite web|first=Justin|last=Style|url=http://www.crossrhythms.co.uk/articles/music/Chevelle_The_Chicago_hard_rock_trio_breaking_big_in_the_mainstream/8257/p1/|title=Chevelle: The Chicago hard rock trio breaking big in the mainstream|work=Crossrhythms.co.uk|date=October 30, 2003|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122163025/https://www.crossrhythms.co.uk/articles/music/Chevelle_The_Chicago_hard_rock_trio_breaking_big_in_the_mainstream/8257/p1/|archive-date=November 22, 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref> Pete started playing guitar and singing and Sam began playing drums in their parents' garage.<ref name="AMG"/> Bassist Matt Scott was in the band until 1996.<ref name="Chevelle Sputnik">{{cite web|url=https://www.sputnikmusic.com/bands/Chevelle/228/|title=Chevelle reviews, music, news|work=[[Sputnikmusic]]|access-date=January 12, 2021}}</ref> Their youngest brother, Joe Loeffler, joined the band replacing Scott.<ref name="AMG"/><ref name="crossrhythms"/> Each member was a self-taught musician.<ref name="crossrhythms"/><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik" /> The name Chevelle came from the band members' passion for fast cars.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Mike|last=Sanders|url=http://loudwire.com/chevelle-frontman-pete-loeffler-hot-rods-hats-off-to-the-bull-more/|title=Chevelle Frontman Pete Loeffler Dishes on Hot Rods, 'Hats Off to the Bull' + More|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=April 26, 2012|access-date=March 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230411055820/http://loudwire.com/chevelle-frontman-pete-loeffler-hot-rods-hats-off-to-the-bull-more/|archive-date=April 11, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> It was also a car their father liked, the [[Chevrolet Chevelle]].<ref name="Christian music">{{Cite web|url=http://christianmusic.com/chevelle/bio.html|title=Chevelle|work=Christian Music|access-date=December 28, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020804153524/http://christianmusic.com/chevelle/bio.html|archive-date=August 4, 2002|url-status=dead}}</ref> The band started playing small outdoor concerts and clubs around [[Chicago, Illinois|Chicago]], [[Illinois]].<ref name="AMG" />

Chevelle recorded a seven-track [[Demo (music)|demo]] known as ''The Blue Album'', released in 1998.<ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/> The band played small concerts for the next three years until they signed with [[Steve Taylor]]'s [[Squint Entertainment]],<ref name="AMG"/><ref name="crossrhythms"/><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/> a [[contemporary Christian music]] label. The band recorded with [[Steve Albini]] for 17 days in [[Electrical Audio]] studios and released its first full-length album, ''[[Point No.&nbsp;1|Point #1]]'' in 1999.<ref name="crossrhythms"/><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/><ref>{{cite journal|last=Olson|first=Chad|date=July–August 1999|title=Album Reviews: Chevelle ''Point #1''|journal=[[HM (magazine)|HM]]|issue=78|issn=1066-6923}}</ref><ref name="JFH#1">{{cite web|first=John|last=DiBase|url=http://www.jesusfreakhideout.com/cdreviews/PointNo1.asp|title=Chevelle, "Point #1" Review|work=Jesus Freak Hideout|date=September 11, 1999|access-date=December 24, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011112235310/http://www.jesusfreakhideout.com/cdreviews/PointNo1.asp|archive-date=November 12, 2001|url-status=live}}</ref> Two singles were released from the album with accompanying music videos, "[[Point No. 1 (song)|Point #1]]" and "Mia".<ref name="crossrhythms"/><ref>{{cite news|first=Steve|last=Knopper|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1999-09-10-9909100222-story.html|title=Chevelle Built On Hard Rock And Brotherly Tolerance|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=September 9, 1999|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://archive.today/20220613033117/https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1999-09-10-9909100222-story.html|archive-date=June 13, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> The songs received [[GMA Dove Award]]s in 2000 and "Point #1" in 2001.<ref name="DOVE_HS">"{{cite web|url=http://www.doveawards.com/history/browse.cfm?cid=32|title=Dove Award Recipients for Hard Music Recorded Song|work=[[Gospel Music Association]]|access-date=November 15, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020106001828/http://www.doveawards.com/history/browse.cfm?cid=32|archive-date=January 6, 2002|url-status=dead}}</ref> The album won "Hard Music Album" in the 2000 Dove Awards.<ref name="DOVE_00">"{{Cite web|url=http://doveawards.com/history/browse.cfm?year=2000|title=Dove Award Recipients for Hard Music Album|work=[[Gospel Music Association]]|access-date=November 15, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020406020434/http://doveawards.com/history/browse.cfm?year=2000|archive-date=April 6, 2002|url-status=dead}}</ref> The album was well received by ''Phantom Tollbooth'' and ''[[HM (magazine)|HM Magazine]]'',<ref name="Tollbooth#1">{{cite web|first=James|last=Stewart|url=http://www.tollbooth.org/review99/chevelle.html|title=Point #1|work=The Phantom Tollbooth|date=July 28, 1999|access-date=December 24, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010224005058/http://www.tollbooth.org/review99/chevelle.html|archive-date=February 24, 2001|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="HM_78">{{Cite journal|first=Chad|last=Olson|url=http://www.hmmagazine.com/issue78/78AlbumReviews.htm|title=Album Reviews: Chevelle Point #1|journal=[[HM (magazine)|HM Magazine]]|date=July–August 1999|access-date=April 24, 2007|issue=78|issn=1066-6923|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010717025343/http://www.hmmagazine.com/issue78/78AlbumReviews.htm|archive-date=July 17, 2001|url-status=dead}}</ref> yet was criticized for its repetitive song structures by Jesus Freak Hideout, a Christian music website.<ref name="JFH#1"/> The band's label was going through legal troubles as [[Word Records]] attempted to wrest control of Squint from Taylor.<ref name="crossrhythms"/> This caused uncertainty with the band's future.<ref name="crossrhythms"/> Discussing the legal battle, bassist Joe Loeffler stated "we weren't sure if anything was going to happen after that, it was pretty crazy."<ref name="crossrhythms"/>

Chevelle toured as support to bands such as [[Sevendust]], [[Machine Head (band)|Machine Head]], [[Filter (band)|Filter]], and [[Powerman 5000]] in this period.<ref name="AMG" /><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik" /> Squint Entertainment closed down in 2001, and the band signed with [[Epic Records]] in 2002.<ref name="AMG"/> In 2002, Chevelle released its second studio album, ''[[Wonder What's Next]],'' on Epic Records.<ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/><ref name="Wonder What's Next AllMusic">{{Cite web|first=Brian|last=O'Neill|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/wonder-whats-next-mw0000224363|title=Wonder What's Next Chevelle|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013148/https://www.allmusic.com/album/wonder-whats-next-mw0000224363|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The band released the single "[[The Red (song)|The Red]]", which reached No.&nbsp;3 on the [[Hot Mainstream Rock Tracks|Mainstream rock charts]], and the video was played in regular rotation on [[MTV]].<ref name="Singles">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/rtt/|title=Chevelle Chart History – Singles|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013150/https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/rtt/|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Wonder What's Next'' peaked at No.&nbsp;14 on the United States [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] album chart.<ref name="Artist Chart History">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/tlp/|title=Chevelle Chart History: Billboard 200|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013148/https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/tlp/|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> Brian O'Neil of [[AllMusic]] stated the album "offers uniqueness not often heard in more commercial fare, no mean feat."<ref name="Wonder What's Next AllMusic"/> Chevelle released two more singles from the album, "[[Closure (Chevelle song)|Closure]]",<ref name="MTV Closure">{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Wiederhorn|url=https://www.mtv.com/news/1479210/chevelle-plan-headlining-tour-are-happy-to-offer-fans-closure/|title=Chevelle Plan Headlining Tour, Are Happy To Offer Fans 'Closure'|work=[[MTV]]|date=September 23, 2003|access-date=July 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927174656/https://www.mtv.com/news/1479210/chevelle-plan-headlining-tour-are-happy-to-offer-fans-closure/|archive-date=September 27, 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> and "[[Send the Pain Below]]",<ref name="MTV Closure"/><ref name="Ozzfest">{{cite latter of which reached the No.&nbsp;1 position on both of the [[Mainstream Rock Chart|mainstream rock]] and [[Modern Rock Tracks chart|modern rock]] charts.<ref name="Singles"/> ''Wonder What's Next'' was certified 2× platinum by the [[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]] with excess sales of one million copies sold in the United States alone in 2003.<ref name="MusicomhreviewWWN">{{cite magazine|first=Tom|last=Day|url=http://www.musicomh.com/albums/chevelle.htm|title=Chevelle – Wonder What's Next (Epic)|magazine=[[MusicOMH]]|date=August 11, 2003|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071107073159/http://www.musicomh.com/albums/chevelle.htm|archive-date=November 7, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&ar=Chevelle&ti=WONDER+WHAT%27S+NEXT#search_section|title=Chevelle – Wonder What's Next (Epic)|work=[[Recording Industry Association of America]]|access-date=January 5, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Chevelle was nominated for three awards at the [[2003 Billboard Music Awards]].<ref name="Billboard Music Awards">{{cite 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> One as a band and two for their song "Send the Pain Below".<ref name="Billboard Music Awards"/> The categories they were nominated for were Modern Rock Artist, Modern Rock Track, and [[Billboard Music Award for Top Rock Song|Top Rock Song]].<ref name="Billboard Music Awards"/>

In 2003, Chevelle performed at [[Ozzfest]],<ref name="Ozzfest"/> where the band recorded and later released its first [[live album]], ''[[Live from the Road]]'',<ref name="Live from the Road">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/68469/chevelle-polishes-live-from-the-road|title=Chevelle Polishes 'Live From The Road'|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=October 24, 2003|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202100917/https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/68469/chevelle-polishes-live-from-the-road|archive-date=December 2, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> and a live [[DVD]], ''Live from the Norva'' on October 14, 2003.<ref name="MTV Closure"/> In 2003, the band was featured on the [[Music as a Weapon Tour|Music as a Weapon II tour]] with [[Disturbed (band)|Disturbed]].<ref name="Live from the Road"/><ref name="Music as a Weapon II AM">{{cite web|first=Johnny|last=Loftus|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/music-as-a-weapon-ii-mw0000322147|title=Music as a Weapon II - Disturbed|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013148/https://www.allmusic.com/album/music-as-a-weapon-ii-mw0000322147|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> On the tour with Disturbed, Chevelle appeared on the tour compilation album, titled ''[[Music as a Weapon Tour#Music as a Weapon II|Music as a Weapon II]]'', featuring the songs "The Red" and "Forfeit".<ref name="Music as a Weapon II AM"/>  Keith Miller of EvangelSociety.org was critical of Chevelle for touring with Ozzfest with bands such as [[Cradle of Filth]], who he claimed incorporated strong Satanic and anti-Christian themes into their lyrics.<ref name="Over-reacter">{{cite web|first=Keith|last=Miller|url=http://www.evangelsociety.org/miller/chevelle2.html|title=Chevelle's Uncertain Witness|work=Evangel Society|date=February 9, 2004|access-date=December 25, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040504092216/http://www.evangelsociety.org/miller/chevelle2.html|archive-date=May 4, 2004|url-status=dead}}</ref> Chevelle held their first major headlining tour, from November 1 to December 17, 2003.<ref name="MTV Closure"/> The tour started in Cleveland and ended in Chicago.<ref name="MTV Closure"/> 

In 2004, Sam Loeffler said, "It's something that's probably going to follow us around forever and that's fine. It's pretty simple. We originally signed with a record company that was backed by [[Word Records|Word]] (a Christian label housing [[John Tesh]] and [[Amy Grant]]), so [''Point #1''] was in Christian bookstores. It was really an accidental thing".<ref name="Over-reacter" /><ref name="Christianity today">{{cite web|first=Andree|last=Farias|url=http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/glimpses/2004/thistypeofthinking.html|title=Chevelle This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In) (Epic)|work=Christianity Today|access-date=December 25, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071218201636/http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/glimpses/2004/thistypeofthinking.html|archive-date=December 18, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> Sam also told the ''Chicago Tribune'', "Our faith is still extremely important to us, but it's also very personal. None of us feels being a rock band on stage should be a pedestal for preaching".<ref name="Live From the Road review">{{cite web|first=Andy|last=Argyrakis|url=http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/reviews/2004/livefromtheroad.html|title=Chevelle Live From the Road (Epic)|work=Christianity Today|access-date=December 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071212062119/http://www.christianitytoday.com/music/reviews/2004/livefromtheroad.html|archive-date=December 12, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Line-up changes, ''This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)'', and ''Vena Sera'' (2004–2008) ===
{{Main|This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)|Vena Sera}}

''[[This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)]]'' was recorded in early 2004, and released on September 21, 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-set-release-date-for-new-album|title=Chevelle Set Release Date For New Album|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=July 13, 2004|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013152/https://blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-set-release-date-for-new-album|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=Melodic>{{cite web|url=http://melodic.net/?page=review&id=2915|title=Melodic Net - Chevelle - This Type of Thinking Could Do Us In|work=[[Melodic (magazine)|Melodic]]|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180906090344/http://melodic.net/?page=review&id=2915|archive-date=September 6, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="This Type AllMusic">{{cite 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013150/https://www.allmusic.com/album/this-type-of-thinking-could-do-us-in-mw0000152819|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The album debuted at No. 8 on the ''Billboard'' 200, and was certified [[RIAA certification|gold]] by the RIAA six weeks later.<ref name="Artist Chart History"/> Johnny Loftus of AllMusic described the songs on the album as "strong dynamically, but sound predetermined — they don't separate from the general loud rock malaise."<ref name="This Type AllMusic"/> The song "[[Vitamin R (Leading Us Along)]]" was released as the first single from the album and reached the No.&nbsp;1 position on the Mainstream Rock chart.<ref name="Singles"/><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.antimusic.com/news/04/dec/item16.shtml|title=Chevelle, Helmet Head SnoCore Tour|work=antiMusic|date=December 23, 2004|access-date=December 24, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050105095618/http://www.antimusic.com/news/04/dec/item16.shtml|archive-date=January 5, 2005|url-status=live}}</ref> Two other singles were released from the album, the titles of which are "[[The Clincher]]" peaking at No. 3 on the Mainstream rock chart, and "[[Panic Prone]]" which peaked at No. 26 on the same chart.<ref name="Singles"/><ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/> The band's song "The Clincher" was featured in the video game ''[[Madden NFL 2005]]''.<ref name="The Clincher soundtrack">{{cite magazine|first=Chris|last=Cook|url=http://www.gameinformer.com/News/Story/200407/N04.0701.1627.08627.htm|title=EA Announces Madden NFL 2005 Soundtrack|magazine=[[Game Informer]]|date=July 1, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/07/01/madden-nfl-2005-busts-out-all-star-musical-line-up|title=Madden NFL 2005 Busts Out All-Star Musical Line-Up|work=[[IGN]]|date=June 17, 2012|access-date=July 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220717002309/https://www.ign.com/articles/2004/07/01/madden-nfl-2005-busts-out-all-star-musical-line-up|archive-date=July 17, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

After the release of the album, Joe Loeffler was dismissed from Chevelle.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/ex-chevelle-bassist-slams-former-bandmates-i-was-fired-plain-and-simple|title=Ex-Chevelle Bassist Slams Former Bandmates: 'I Was Fired, Plain And Simple'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=July 7, 2005|access-date=June 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171213005327/https://blabbermouth.net/news/ex-chevelle-bassist-slams-former-bandmates-i-was-fired-plain-and-simple|archive-date=December 13, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Did Joe get fired">{{cite web|url=http://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/general_music_news/chevelle_bassist_fired.html|title=Chevelle Bassist Fired?|work=[[Ultimate Guitar]]|date=July 4, 2005|access-date=December 24, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070503232838/https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/news/general_music_news/chevelle_bassist_fired.html|archive-date=May 3, 2007|url-status=live}}</ref> Due to different stories from the band members, it is unclear whether he was fired or left the band of his own accord.<ref name="Did Joe get fired"/> Pete and Sam stated the following on the band's official website: "After three years of non-stop touring and recording, Joe is taking a break to be home with family. We'll miss having him on the road with us, but as his brothers and bandmates we respect his decision and are looking forward to getting out there and playing for the fans. See you on tour." However, according to [[Ultimate Guitar Archive]], Joe said he was fired.<ref name="Did Joe get fired"/>

The band supported ''This Type of Thinking (Could Do Us In)'' with a headlining tour that included opening acts such as [[Taproot (band)|Taproot]] and [[Thirty Seconds to Mars]],<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/chevelle-taproot-team-for-summer-tour-62604/|title=Chevelle, Taproot Team For Summer Tour|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=June 13, 2005|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211122161152/https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/chevelle-taproot-team-for-summer-tour-62604/|archive-date=November 22, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Harris|url=https://www.mtv.com/news/1503823/chevelle-taproot-30-seconds-to-mars-map-out-summer-tour/|title=Chevelle, Taproot, 30 Seconds To Mars Map Out Summer Tour|work=[[MTV]]|date=June 9, 2005|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160412142151/https://www.mtv.com/news/1503823/chevelle-taproot-30-seconds-to-mars-map-out-summer-tour/|archive-date=April 12, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and continued playing small tours in 2005 with [[Geno Lenardo]] from the band [[Filter (band)|Filter]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-lineup-change-for-upcoming-tour|title=Chevelle: Lineup Change For Upcoming Tour|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=June 30, 2005|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220613045029/https://blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-lineup-change-for-upcoming-tour|archive-date=June 13, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> In August 2005, the Loeffler brothers' brother-in-law, Dean Bernardini, joined the band as their bassist.<ref name="AMG" /><ref name="Did Joe get fired" /> In 2006, Chevelle supported [[Nickelback]] for an arena tour across the United States.<ref name="Did Joe get fired"/>

[[File:Pete Loeffler at 2007 MyCokeFest in Atlanta.JPG|thumb|Vocalist and guitarist Pete Loeffler performing in 2007 at MyCokeFest in Atlanta]]

In 2006, the band recorded their fourth studio album, ''[[Vena Sera]]''. The album was the first Chevelle recorded with Bernardini.<ref name="Vena Sera AllMusic">{{cite web|first=Corey|last=Apar|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/vena-sera-mw0000746725|title=Vena Sera Chevelle|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013147/https://www.allmusic.com/album/vena-sera-mw0000746725|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Vena Sera'' was released on April 3, 2007,<ref name="Vena Sera AllMusic"/><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Michael|last=Endelman|url=https://ew.com/article/2007/03/30/vena-sera/|title=Vena Sera Review|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|date=April 6, 2007|access-date=June 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070421010156/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,20016445,00.html|archive-date=April 21, 2007|url-status=live}}</ref> debuting at No.&nbsp;12 on the ''Billboard'' 200, and sold 62,000 copies during its first week of release.<ref name="Chevelle Sputnik" /><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Katie|last=Hasty|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1052919/now-24-trumps-duff-mcbride-timbaland-at-no-1|title=Now 24 Trumps Duff, McBride, Timbaland at No. 1|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=April 11, 2007|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130414015239/http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1052919/now-24-trumps-duff-mcbride-timbaland-at-no-1|archive-date=April 14, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> The title of the album translates to "vein liquid" in Latin, representing the blood Chevelle put into making the album, according to Pete.<ref name="Journal">{{Cite web|first=Sam|last=Loeffler|url=http://www.chevelleinc.com/bandnotes_content.html|title=Band notes|publisher=Chevelle|access-date=December 25, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071208100937/http://www.chevelleinc.com/bandnotes_content.html|archive-date=December 8, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Corey Apar of AllMusic states that "''Vena Sera'' probably won't disappoint fans, and it didn't, if for the sole fact that it basically sounds just like Chevelle's other albums". He noted that the song "I Get It" "has a relatively lighter underbelly than the rest, which is a nice change of pace, but it's ultimately too little, too late".<ref name="Vena Sera AllMusic"/> "[[Well Enough Alone]]", the first single from the album, was written about the departure of Joe Loeffler, and reached No.&nbsp;4 on the Mainstream rock charts.<ref name="Singles"/> Chevelle toured with [[Evanescence]] and [[Finger Eleven]] during March and April 2007,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/evanescence-chevelle-finger-eleven-tour-dates-announced|title=Evanescence, Chevelle, Finger Eleven: Tour Dates Announced|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=January 19, 2007|access-date=January 5, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220613043755/https://blabbermouth.net/news/evanescence-chevelle-finger-eleven-tour-dates-announced|archive-date=June 13, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> followed by a headlining tour with Finger Eleven and [[Strata (band)|Strata]] in May and June.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-extends-tour-into-june|title=Chevelle Extends Tour Into June|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=April 30, 2007|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126101953/https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-extends-tour-into-june/|archive-date=November 26, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The second single from the album, "[[I Get It]]", was released on June 12, 2007, and a video for the song debuted on MTV on November 27, 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/videos/chevelle/192012/i-get-it.jhtml#artist=509055|title=Chevelle I Get It – Premiere videos|work=[[MTV]]|date=November 27, 2007|access-date=December 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090114214553/http://www.mtv.com/videos/chevelle/192012/i-get-it.jhtml|archive-date=January 14, 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> In July of the same year, Chevelle toured Australia as a supporting act for the band [[The Butterfly Effect (band)|The Butterfly Effect]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/the-butterfly-effect-imago-to-receive-u-s-release|title=The Butterfly Effect: 'Imago' To Receive U.S. Release|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=October 9, 2007|access-date=June 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143417/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/the-butterfly-effect-imago-to-receive-u-s-release/|archive-date=June 12, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> On the tour in Australia, Chevelle's band manager Rose died of cancer, much to the distress of the band.<ref name="Journal"/>

On May 9, 2007, during a show in [[Fort Worth, Texas]] Chevelle's trailer containing all of the band's equipment was stolen from the hotel at which the members were staying.<ref name="Fort Worth">{{cite web|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=74673|title=Chevelle slowly recovering stonlen gear|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=June 14, 2007|access-date=August 12, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080514131213/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=74673|archive-date=May 14, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> The band posted a notice saying, "Most items are labeled 'Chevelle' and if you notice anything suspicious on [[eBay]] or other online resellers selling 'authentic' Chevelle items... guitar, basses, drums, amplifiers, risers, backdrops, tee shirts... please call the police..." A month later in an interview, Sam Loeffler stated, "Of the 14 guitars, we got two of 'em, and then we got some amplifiers back and our monitor system. So it's really, I mean it's cool because it's kind of like Christmas, only really weird. People have been calling us and saying, 'Hey, I bought this or that', and you know, we're just doing our best to buy it back from them. And certainly the issue is not a money issue, it's about having the pieces of gear that you did all your records with."<ref name="Fort Worth"/>

=== ''Sci-Fi Crimes'' and ''Hats Off to the Bull'' (2009–2012) ===
{{Main|Sci-Fi Crimes|Hats Off to the Bull}}

[[File:Pete of Chevelle Live at the Carnival of Madness 2012.JPG|thumb|upright|Pete Loeffler performing live at the Carnival of Madness tour in 2012 at the Laredo Energy Arena]]
In 2009, Chevelle entered a studio in [[Nashville, Tennessee|Nashville]], [[Tennessee]] with producer Brian Virtue. Sam Loeffler stated, "We have spent a lot of time making these songs something different from past records without losing the core of our passion. We are a hard rock, melodic band and it's still what drives us as musicians."<ref name="Fifthystuff">{{cite web|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=114802|title=Chevelle: Video footage from the studio posted online|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=February 20, 2009|access-date=December 27, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090312122822/http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=114802|archive-date=March 12, 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> The new album, titled ''[[Sci-Fi Crimes]]'' was released on August 31, 2009,<ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Coplan|url=https://consequence.net/2009/08/chevelle-new-touralbum-to-be-so-good-its-criminal/|title=Chevelle new tour/album to be so good it's criminal|work=[[Consequence (publication)|Consequence]]|date=August 23, 2009|access-date=January 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220717002309/https://consequence.net/2009/08/chevelle-new-touralbum-to-be-so-good-its-criminal/|archive-date=July 17, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="HM Sci-Fi Crimes">{{cite magazine|first=Doug|last=Van Pelt|url=https://hmmagazine.com/chevelle-announce-sci-fi-crimes-tour/|title=Chevelle Announce Sci-Fi Crimes Tour|magazine=[[HM (magazine)|HM]]|date=August 20, 2009|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305075654/https://hmmagazine.com/chevelle-announce-sci-fi-crimes-tour/|archive-date=March 5, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> peaking at No.&nbsp;6 on the ''Billboard'' 200 album chart with sales of about 46,000, the highest entry onto the chart to date for the band.<ref name="Chevelle Sputnik"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=126673|title=Chevelle's 'Sci-Fi Crimes' Cracks U.S. Top 10|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=September 9, 2009|access-date=July 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141224164300/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-s-sci-fi-crimes-cracks-u-s-top/|archive-date=December 24, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="anylastwords">{{Cite web|url=http://legacy.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=148614|title=Chevelle to release Any Last Words? DVD|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=October 31, 2010|access-date=May 18, 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130201201836/http://legacy.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=148614|archive-date=February 1, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> The album was praised by Jared Johnson of AllMusic for taking a step in a new direction in regards to the lyrics.<ref name="Sci-fi Crimes AllMusic">{{cite web|first=Jared|last=Johnson|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/sci-fi-crimes-r1626372/review|title=Sci-fi Crimes|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101205130331/http://www.allmusic.com/album/sci-fi-crimes-r1626372/review|archive-date=December 5, 2010|url-status=live}}</ref> Pete Loeffler normally wrote lyrics about personal subjects, however on ''Sci-Fi Crimes'', he wrote of stories including apparitions, conspiracy theories, and erratic sleeping conditions.<ref name="Sci-fi Crimes AllMusic"/> The tour following the release of ''Sci-Fi Crimes'' was in the late 2009.<ref name="HM Sci-Fi Crimes"/> [[Halestorm]] opened for Chevelle on this tour.<ref name="HM Sci-Fi Crimes"/> Chevelle also joined Halestorm, [[Staind]], and [[Shinedown]] on "Stimulate This!" tour starting in July 2009.<ref name="Halestorm opening for Chevelle">{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/staind-shinedown-chevelle-halestorm-to-team-up-for-stimulate-this-tour|title=Staind, Shinedown, Chevelle, Halestorm To Team Up For 'Stimulate This!' Tour|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=May 11, 2009|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150920214447/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/staind-shinedown-chevelle-halestorm-to-team-up-for-stimulate-this-tour/|archive-date=September 20, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

In January 2011, Chevelle released a live CD/DVD combo, ''Any Last Words''.<ref name="anylastwords"/> The release was part of Chevelle's ten-year anniversary as a recording band. As a special offer for fans, part of the pre-order package included a T-shirt and the fans' name in the 'thank yous' part of the album booklet.<ref name="anylastwords"/>

On December 6, 2011, Chevelle released ''[[Hats Off to the Bull]]'', their sixth studio album.<ref name="Hats Off to the Bull AllMusic">{{cite web|first=Gregory|last=Heaney|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/hats-off-to-the-bull-r2334528/review|title=Hats Off to the Bull Chevelle|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521215057/https://www.allmusic.com/album/hats-off-to-the-bull-mw0002253896|archive-date=May 21, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Pete|last=Crigler|url=http://www.popmatters.com/pm/review/152484-chevelle-hats-off-to-the-bull/|title=Chevelle-Hats Off to the Bull|magazine=[[PopMatters]]|date=January 4, 2012|access-date=July 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120109032353/http://www.popmatters.com/pm/review/152484-chevelle-hats-off-to-the-bull/|archive-date=January 9, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> The album's first single was titled "[[Face to the Floor]]",<ref name="hatsoffdebut">{{cite web|url=http://legacy.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=167236|title=Chevelle's 'Hats Off to the Bull' crack U.S. Top 20|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=February 1, 2013|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130201111054/http://legacy.roadrunnerrecords.com/blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=167236|archive-date=February 1, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Liz|last=Ramanand|url=https://loudwire.com/chevelle-face-to-the-floor-song-review/|title=Chevelle, ‘Face to the Floor’ – Song Review|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=September 29, 2011|access-date=August 15, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240719154213/https://loudwire.com/chevelle-face-to-the-floor-song-review/|archive-date=July 19, 2024|url-status=dead}}</ref> which reached No. 3 on ''Billboard'''s Rock songs chart.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/|title=Chevelle Active Rock|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=January 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105013153/https://www.billboard.com/artist/chevelle/chart-history/|archive-date=January 5, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The album debuted at No.&nbsp;20 on the ''Billboard'' charts and sold 43,000 copies in its first week of release.<ref name="hatsoffdebut"/> Joe Barresi, who produced ''Hats Off to the Bull'' said of the album, "Rather than simply subscribing to a tried-and-true formula, they made a conscious effort to incorporate new sounds and textures into their patented airtight anthems. As a result, ''Hats Off to the Bull'' is one of the group's most infectious and impressive offerings to date."<ref name="hatsoffdebut"/> AllMusic reviewer Gregory Heaney stated the album is "Heavy and dramatic, the album is packed full of tightly coiled, muscular riffs, giving the album a controlled feeling more like a slow burn than an explosive, cathartic release."<ref name="Hats Off to the Bull AllMusic"/>

Chevelle was nominated for Rock Band of the Year at the 2012 Loudwire Music Awards.<ref name="Loudwire Music Awards 2012">{{cite web|url=https://loudwire.com/rock-band-of-the-year-2012-loudwire-music-awards/|title=Rock Band of the Year – 2012|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=December 4, 2012|access-date=January 11, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201127094334/https://loudwire.com/rock-band-of-the-year-2012-loudwire-music-awards/|archive-date=November 27, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Also, a compilation album of band favorites called ''[[Stray Arrows: A Collection of Favorites]]'', was released to stores on December 4, 2012.<ref name="Stray Arrows">{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Colgan|url=https://metalinsider.net/new-music/new-noteworthy-december-4th-same-old-trip|title=New & Noteworthy December 4th: Same Old Trip|work=Metal Insider|date=December 4, 2012|access-date=July 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220716054730/https://metalinsider.net/new-music/new-noteworthy-december-4th-same-old-trip|archive-date=July 16, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Stray Arrows Loudwire">{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Bowar|url=https://loudwire.com/chevelle-greatest-hits-compilation-album-stray-arrows-december/|title=Chevelle to Release Greatest Hits Compilation Album 'Stray Arrows' in December|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=November 6, 2012|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220612062944/https://loudwire.com/chevelle-greatest-hits-compilation-album-stray-arrows-december/|archive-date=June 12, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Stray Arrows Allmusic">{{cite web|first=Gregory|last=Heaney|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/mw0002443034|title=Stray Arrows: A Collection of Favorites - Chevelle|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=January 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220531114529/https://www.allmusic.com/album/mw0002443034|archive-date=May 31, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> The compilation includes 11 songs and a previously unreleased track titled "Fizgig".<ref name="Stray Arrows"/><ref name="Stray Arrows Loudwire"/><ref name="Stray Arrows Allmusic"/> The [[Best Buy]] version has 15 songs and the track "Fizgig".<ref name="Stray Arrows"/>

=== ''La Gárgola'', ''The North Corridor'' and departure of Dean Bernardini (2013–2019) ===
{{Main|La Gárgola|The North Corridor}}
After wrapping up touring in support of ''Hats off to the Bull'' in 2013, Chevelle entered the studio to record their seventh album, re-teaming with [[Joe Barresi]] to produce the album.<ref name="banana1015">{{cite web|first=Tree|last=Riddle|url=http://banana1015.com/chevelle-drop-new-single-listen-to-take-out-the-gunman-audio/|title=Chevelle Drop New Single, Listen to 'Take Out The Gunman' [Audio]|work=Banana 101.5|date=February 3, 2014|access-date=June 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114153516/http://banana1015.com/chevelle-drop-new-single-listen-to-take-out-the-gunman-audio/|archive-date=January 14, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> Recording and production finished early in 2014, and the band announced on February 1 that the album, to be released April 1, 2014, would be titled ''[[La Gárgola]]'' (Spanish for "the gargoyle").<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.antimusic.com/news/14/February/05Chevelle_Reveal_First_Song_From_New_Album.shtml|title=Chevelle Reveal First Song From New Album|work=antiMusic|date=February 5, 2014|access-date=February 7, 2014}}</ref><ref name="blabbermouth123">{{cite web|url=https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-la-gargola-artwork-track-listing-revealed/|title=Chevelle: 'La Gargola' Artwork, Track Listing Revealed|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=February 25, 2014|access-date=January 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211127171201/https://www.blabbermouth.net/news/chevelle-la-gargola-artwork-track-listing-revealed/|archive-date=November 27, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Colgan|url=http://www.metalinsider.net/columns/new-noteworthy-april-1st-one-more-for-the-road|title=New & Noteworthy, April 1st: One more for the road|work=Metal Insider|date=April 1, 2014|access-date=April 5, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407070819/http://www.metalinsider.net/columns/new-noteworthy-april-1st-one-more-for-the-road|archive-date=April 7, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> Lead singer Pete Loeffler describes that the album is about "the dark underbelly of American culture."<ref>{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Niesel|url=https://www.clevescene.com/cleveland/band-of-brothers-chevelle-regroups-for-la-gargola-its-best-album-yet/Content?oid=4350906|title=Band of Brothers: Chevelle Regroups for La Gargola, its Best Album Yet|work=Cleveland Scene|date=August 6, 2014|access-date=September 20, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141012073645/https://www.clevescene.com/cleveland/band-of-brothers-chevelle-regroups-for-la-gargola-its-best-album-yet/Content?oid=4350906|archive-date=October 12, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> The first single from the album, titled "[[Take Out the Gunman]]", was released on February 3, 2014.<ref name="banana1015"/><ref>{{cite magazine|first=David|last=Stagg|url=https://hmmagazine.com/listen-chevelle-release-new-song-take-gunman/|title=Listen: Chevelle releases new song, 'Take Out the Gunman'|magazine=[[HM (magazine)|HM]]|date=February 3, 2014|access-date=July 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220716054730/https://hmmagazine.com/listen-chevelle-release-new-song-take-gunman/|archive-date=July 16, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Childers|url=https://loudwire.com/chevelle-take-out-the-gunman-lyric-video/|title=Chevelle Unveil ‘Take Out the Gunman’ Lyric Video|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=February 20, 2014|access-date=August 15, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140803091510/https://loudwire.com/chevelle-take-out-the-gunman-lyric-video/|archive-date=August 3, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> The other singles from the album are "[[Hunter Eats Hunter (song)|Hunter Eats Hunter]]" and "[[An Island (Chevelle song)|An Island]]".<ref>{{cite
